back.name: Thieves in the Night
back.text:
A thunderous crash reverberates through the air, accompanied by a gale of cold wind that chills you to your bones---and then, silence. “They’re here,” whispers Maddalena’s voice. You haven't known her long, but you recognize the tone of her voice---a pure, unmitigated dread that speaks volumes.
Each remaining investigator is defeated.

back.name: The Long Quiet
back.text:
Once through the void, you inexplicably find yourself on a small island, lost in a dark sea. You are in some kind of open-air temple with a brazier burning brightly at the center of the stone floor. Maddalena sits in deep concentration, the white owl perched on her shoulder. “Welcome to my home,” she says, matter-of-factly. “I hope now you understand the gravity of our situation.” You’re furious. Maddalena's cryptic explanations have helped you understand very little, except that she has drawn you against your will into a deadly plot; one that has endangered not only the both of you, but all of Arkham---and possibly the world beyond. For her part, Maddalena just chuckles miserably at your rage and her misfortune. “Very well, then. I’ll make sure you understand completely. The Sorrows know we’re here and will send their thralls across time to find us. I can prevent their entry easily as long as I remain undisturbed, but if you can seal their entrances to my sanctuary, it will guarantee our survival. And perhaps, you’ll learn just how terrible they truly are.”
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Gather the 6 set-aside Reflection locations and place 2 next to each Primordial location, revealed. Until the end of the scenario, each Primordial location is connected to the 2 Reflection locations next to it (and vice-versa.) Put this card next to the Agenda deck, as a reminder. Put Maddalena Talenti into play at The Long Quiet. Gather the set-aside deck of Reflection enemies and the Shattered Reflections story card and set them next to the Agenda deck.

front.text:
Maddalena's words echo in your mind as you race to keep up with the white owl. "This is the Astral Plane," she says. "The realm of quintessence, and of the soul. Here, I hold power strong enough to keep you safe. But we are not alone---three great evils from the dawn of time pursue us. The Three Mothers---Tenebrarum, Suspiriorum, and Lachrymarum. The Sorrows. The primordial storm through which we now walk is their birthplace." You shield your eyes from the pounding rain as you shout up to the owl above. Wouldn't that mean that these Sorrows---whoever they are---wield power here, as well? "Yes," the voice replies. "So we keep moving."

front.text:
Jinxed. Veiled.
Increase the cost of the first card you play at <name> during your turn by 1.

You dodge the violent, clawing shadows snapping at your heels and push upward toward the great spiraling void. “Servants of the Sorrows,” Maddalena explains as her owl soars through the giant hole. “This realm is a prison for the souls of their prey.” Out of breath, you wonder aloud---why you? Why are the Sorrows after you? What does any of this have to do with you? For the first time, Maddalena’s voice falters. “I… thought I would need help. Of all the people in Arkham, I learned of you and your exploits. I believed no one else would have been capable to contend against them, and was... too eager. Yet, now, in my haste… I appear to have damned us both.” Her voice falls silent for a moment before regaining its usual commanding tone. “Come. You’re almost there. Enter the void.”
Put The Long Quiet into play and move each investigator there. Flip this card back over.

front.text:
A thousand questions blaze in your mind as you slog through the sandbanks of the ancient sea. Why are these "Sorrows" after you? Who is this woman, guiding you through this bizarre place? "I am a servant of Aradia di Tuscano, breaker of shackles and daughter of the goddess Diana," says Maddalena's voice. "The Sorrows have been enemies of my lady for eons. As I said, they hold immense power here in the Astral Plane. But on Earth, their strength is tethered to their lairs---places of great significance to them. For reasons I do not know, for the first time in a millennium, each of the Three Mothers had left her lair and converged upon your Arkham. I moved against them, and... misjudged their stength."

back.name: Chorus
back.text:
Amalia's voice rises, a siren's wail building to a piercing crescendo that reverberates through every crumbling corner of the sinking theatre. The Rhine Maidens join in, creating a chaotic, haunting melody that threatens to drive you mad.
Find each enemy in The Depths and spawn it in the location where the investigators began at this level of The Deluge. Each investigator must test (3). <obj> If Amalia Verdi is defeated: Advance.
front.flavor_text: Amalia emerges onto the sunken stage, a blurry figure amidst all the rain. A terrible, desperate realization settles over you. Amalia must be under the sway of Mater Lachrymarum, or perhaps something worse-- a willing vessel for the Mother of Tears herself. If you want to survive this night, you know what you have to do.

back.name: The Rain, Ending
back.text:
Amalia falls backward into the churning waves. The siren song dies in her throat, cut off mid-note, her face frozen in an expression of agony and disbelief. Then, almost instantly, the theatre begins to buckle, collapsing under the weight of the endless rain. Like a rat scrambling to escape a sinking ship, you claw toward the exits, driven by sheer panic as the waves beat against your body. Each step forward feels like a futile struggle, the knowledge gnawing at you that beyond the theatre doors lies only more of this watery nightmare---a city swallowed whole by the sea. but as you burst through, gasping for air, you stumble out onto the street. The rain has stopped, the air is warm, and the city is unchanged. The Teatro di San Carlo stands behind you, proud and gleaming in the light of a rising sun. The horror has vanished, and yet, your freedom tastes bitter---like your survival is a cruel joke.
R2

back.name: Third Verse
back.text:

Find the Chorus enemy in The Depths with the least amount of resource tokens, and spawn it in the location where the investigators began at this level of The Deluge. If they do not, the Rhine Maidens pull that investigator beneath the waves; that investigator manages to free themself, but suffers 1 physical trauma.

front.flavor_text:
Desperation and panic are causing you to lose your wits, to doubt yourself. 
Amalia has to be a prisoner of Mater Lachrymarum-- a victim of forces out of her control, like you. Maybe you haven't given enough of yourself to the Mother of Tears. Maybe you can convince her that you deserve to live.

back.name: The Pain, Unending
back.text:
Your worst memories rise unbidden. The sorrows that shaped you, the regret that has followed you for years: they are the price of your freedom. Slowly, you release them. One by one, your memories slip away, carried by the surging tide. Each one leaves you a little lighter, but so too do you feel the shape of their absence as they are stolen away to be woven into this realm's endless tapestry of sorrow. And then, you are standing at center stage of the Teatro di San Carlo, restored and pristine. Amalia gasps for breath on her hands and knees before you, wide-eyed with wonder and disbelief. You've all escaped-- but something of you remains behind, taken by the Mother of Tears.
R1.

back.name: Grand Finale
back.text:
The Theatre reverberates as the flood reaches its apex. You are washed away, pulled beneath the rising tide. And even now, as you sink, drowning in the grief-stricken waters of Mater Lachrymarum's world, Amalia's song continues.
Each remaining investigator is defeated.

back.text:
Chased by the shadowy sirens that lie beneath the waves, you push yourself harder against the tide. If only there was some sign, anything at all, that might help you find your way out of this horrible place?
Find the Chorus enemy in The Depths with the least amount of resource tokens, and spawn it in the location where the investigators began at this level of The Deluge. The Lead investigator must decide: Listen to Amalia's lyrics, there might be something useful hidden in them. Attach the Burden Weakness nearest to your location not at The Monument to the Mother to The Monument to the Mother. Put 1 resource token on each Chorus enemy. Tell everyone to shut out Amalia's voice! You suffer no effects.

front.flavor_text: As the waters climb higher and higher, the Teatro di San Carlo slowly sinks beneath the waves. Amalia Verdi's haunting song drifts from somewhere deep within the opera house, undeterred by the rising tide. Maybe you're not much of an opera fan after all.

back.name: The Rain, Unending
back.text:
You lay down your burdens before the statue. There's a sudden flash of blinding light, and when your sight returns, the churning waters have receded slightly---but outside, the rain pounds down harder than ever.
Set each location in play aside, out of play. Investigators are not defeated during this process. Move each Chorus enemy in play to The Depths. Shuffle each other enemy back into the encounter deck. (If an enemy weakness is in play, place it on top of its investigator's deck, face down.) Increase the Deluge level by 1. If the current Deluge level is 4 or higher, put the Sunken Theatre location into play face up and spawn Amalia Verdi at the Sunken Theatre. Then, perform the following: Each investigator who is not at The Monument to the Mother is swallowed by the rising tide and is defeated. Each surviving investigator loses each of their clues. Shuffle each Burden weakness in play back into the Deck of Burdens. Draw a random set-aside location other than The Monument to the Mother, put it into play, and place each surviving investigator at that location. Put The Monument to the Mother and 4 other random set-aside locations into play, face up. Attach a card from the Deck of Burdens to each location other than The Monument to the Mother, face down. If Amalia Verdi is in play, advance to both set aside versions of Act 2. Both are in play. Otherwise, flip this act back over. Continue your escape from the Teatro di San Carlo.

front.flavor_text: Nussbaum Academy for the Performing Arts was founded in the late 1890s by Helena Nussbaum, a wealthy and eccentric immigrant from Baden-Württemberg. Over the years the academy has earned wide international acclaim, with alumni featured in the London Symphony Orchestra and the Ballets Russes---but based on the state of affairs this evening, it's safe to say you're witnessing the Academy's final act.

back.name: A Final Bow
back.text:
Somewhere in the academy, a grandfather clock tolls---once, twice, three times. Silence hangs heavy in the air. Then, without warning, one of the nearby bewitched students freezes in place. Her arms hang limply in the air like a marionette for what seems like an eternity, before the girl lets out a bloodcurdling scream, her eyes wide with terror. That sound triggers a chain reaction. Soon, another student joins in, then another, until the entire school erupts in a cacophony of horror. The shrieks claw at your sanity, a twisted symphony of despair that you can’t escape. It’s too much to bear, and your fear and instinct take over. You bolt for the exit, hands pressed against your ears, desperate to drown out the nightmare.
Add 1 to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. Each remaining investigator is defeated.

front.flavor_text: You had expected bedlam inside of Nussbaum Academy as the fire rages upstairs, but the scene that greets you inside is horrifying. The lifeless bodies of students lie sprawled throughout the grand mansion, and the few who are still conscious wander aimlessly from room to room, trapped in an unbreakable trance. What terrible witchcraft has happened here?

back.name: Deadly Inheritance
back.text:
The atmosphere of chaos enveloping the academy seems to freeze as you hear the sound of heels clicking against the tiles behind you. At the far end of the hall is Ana Giuliano, the elegant grande dame from that notorious night at the Hotel Seasons, indifferent to the flames consuming the academy around her. "So," she purrs, "We finally meet face-to-face. I trust your recovery has been satisfactory?" Madame Giuliano laughs throatily as she sizes you up, her arms folded across her chest. "Unfortunately, your timing couldn't be more inconvenient. I'm here to collect on a debt owed by my sister, and there are matters to settle before I can take what's mine. Clearing the building of vermin, for instance." A distant scream pierces the school's eerie silence, sudden and jarring. The tension shatters, and Madame Giuliano seizes the moment. She slips quickly away down the hall to the Headmistress' Chambers, her taunting voice echoing back to you. "Find me below when you tire of playing games, darling. I'll be waiting for you."
Put The Chamber of Sighs into play, revealed. Gather the set-aside Vivat Regina encounter set and put Ana Giuliano into play at the Chamber of Sighs with 2 resource tokens (from the token bank) on her as barrier tokens (3, if there are 3 or more investigators.) Reveal each unrevealed location in play other than the Headmistress' Chambers. Then, search all set-aside cards and the victory display for the Elite Sarah Pierce, Olga Safronova, and Patricia Simms enemies, and spawn them in the The Greenhouse, The Natatorium, and the Dining Hall. Attach one of the Binding Charm treacheries to each of these enemies. Shuffle each copy of Queenly Majesty into the encounter deck, along with the encounter discard pile. Ana Giuliano's maximum barrier value is 2 (3, if there are 3 or more investigators.) Put this card next to the agenda deck as a reminder.

front.text: <obj> If investigators at a location connected to the Headmistress' Chambers have at least 2 keys: You may choose to advance.
front.flavor_text: You're itching to get into the Headmistress' chambers, but her door is much sturdier than it looks. Maybe one of the students can help you find a key, if you can find any who still have their wits about them.

back.name: Sur les Pointes
back.text:
Once inside the Headmistress' chambers, you scour every nook and cranny, searching for any clue about Madame Giuliano. The minutes pass in silence until Gigi gasps. "I only just touched it," she says, pointing to an ornate wall carving of a blue flower. A hidden panel has opened beside her, revealing a dark passage. "D'you wanna see where it goes?" You both venture down a long, winding tunnel toward a faint, distant light. Eventually, you arrive at your destination---and wish you hadn't. Several women in robes encircle an open chamber, the lifeless body of a young woman contorted in agony at their center. An older, dark-skinned woman in a stylish suit---clearly their leader---paces over the corpse. "It's not enough," she laments, frustration coloring her voice. "There aren't enough suitable candidates for Helena's arrival. What will she say? We're running out of time." The leader whirls around to her followers, her eyes burning with rage. "We continue the sacrifices! The students must die! Helena, give me power---AAGH!" The sudden outburst startles you, and you realize Gigi has set the velvet curtains surrounding the room's perimeter on fire with a nearby candelabra. "I've had enough of this witchy nonsense," she hisses, her eyes blazing as flames spread throughout the chamber. "Let's get out of here!"
Reveal Headmistress' Chambers. Put the Chamber of Sighs into play, revealed, and move each investigator at a location adjacent to the Headmistress' Chambers to the Headmistress' Chambers. Discard cards from the top of the encounter deck until two Witch enemies are revealed. Spawn one at the Chamber of Sighs, and the other at the Performance Hall. Then, Spin the Performance Hall until its top and bottom exits are facing each Academy location at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions. Gather the set-aside Blanche Pappenheimer enemy and put her into play at The Chamber of Sighs. Shuffle the Inferno encounter set into the encounter deck, along with the discard pile.

front.text: <obj> At the end of the round, investigators may spend the requisite amount of clues as a group to advance.
front.flavor_text:
Thanks to Gigi's foresight, slipping into Nussbaum Academy is a breeze. If there's any dirt on Madame Giuliano here, finding it should be a walk in the park; if you didn't know better, you'd think school was out for the season.
So why can't you shake this nagging feeling of unease?

back.name: Pas de Chat
back.text:
It quickly becomes apparent that all is not well within the prestigious dance academy. An eerie tension hangs in the air, and the sense of dread in the back of your mind has only grown larger. Though Gigi's ruse was vital in clearing out most of the students, the ones you encounter now are dazed and confused, moving languidly from room to room like sleepwalkers. Strangely, you've encountered no signs of the school's faculty. The Headmistress's chambers, you realize, could hold vital clues about Madame Giuliano's whereabouts, but they are securely locked, much like many other rooms dedicated to the school's staff. As you test the Headmistress's door, a small, glassy object tumbles down a nearby staircase, landing with a delicate thud. You pick it up and find it's an intricately carved bird in crystal. You crane your neck upward to see where it might have fallen from, but the top of the stairway is shrouded in darkness.
Choose an investigator to take control of the set-aside Glass Peacock story asset. Until the end of the scenario, this card does not take up a hand slot. Reveal any remaining unrevealed Academy locations except for the Headmistress' Chambers. Gather the set-aside Patricia Simms, Olga Safronova, and Sarah Pierce story assets. Put Patricia Simms into play at the Lecture Theatre, Olga Safronova at the Private Recital Chamber, and Sarah Pierce at the Student Dormitory.

back.name: Grande Reverence
back.text:
Despite the nightmarish horrors you'd witnessed this evening, Ana Giuliano's command of the eldritch arts catches you by surprise. She swiftly counters your attacks with an imperceptible barrier, and her own barrage of withering spells inflict searing pain on you and your companions. Yet, through sheer tenacity---or a stroke of luck---you manage to gradually wear down her defenses in an intense and grueling battle. With her back to the wall, Madame Giuliano starts to laugh---a soft, self-satisfied chuckle that swells, growing louder and louder until it transforms into the howling cackle of a madwoman.

back.name: Suspiriorum
back.text:
You tear through the dimly lit halls of Nussbaum Academy, the manic cackling of Madame Pappenheimer's coven snapping at your heels. With one final sprint, you and Gigi crash through the front doors, spilling out into the cold night. You don't stop running until the academy is a distant silhouette against the moonlit sky, the coven's furious cries fading into the darkness.
R1

front.text:
“Step aside, toots,” Gigi says, tired of Patricia’s hysterics. She steps up, her voice sharp and cutting. “Listen here, Missy! You think you’re the first little girl to ever be scared of somethin’? Well, I’ve got news for you!” Something about the shrill, nasal edge of Gigi’s voice as she berates the girl manages to slice through Patricia’s trance. Dazed, Patricia blinks, then thanks you both for pulling her out of it. She quickly tells you about a secret key to the Headmistress’ office that she's tucked away, in case you can help save Madame Pappenheimer from whatever horrors have overcome the school. As Patricia runs off, Gigi smirks, self-satisfied. “See?” she says. “Nothin’ to it!”
Gather one of the set-aside keys and put it three locations away from you counter-clockwise (skipping the Headmistress' Chambers). Remember that you may use a action to pick up a key on a location with no clues on it. Flip this card over and add Patricia Simms to the victory display.

With some effort, you manage to snap Sarah out of her trance. Her voice is raspy and hoarse, worn thin from hours spent singing a haunting, mournful melody she can barely recall. You urge her to get out of the school---fast. “But wait,” she whispers, her voice tiny and strained. “If you need to find the Headmistress, I’ve hidden a key where no one else will think to look…”

<center>Through us do you know fear.
Through us it was, by languishing desires, that you worshipped and prayed to the wormy grave. Holy was the grave to you; lovely was its darkness; saintly its corruption.
Yes, you, young coward. 
We take you now to our heart, and season you for what is to come.
Banish the frailties of hope.

back.name: Encroaching Shadow
back.text:
The sadness here is palpable, filling your mind with distant regrets you can’t quite name. Every surface, every shadowed alcove, feels like it’s mired in centuries of regret and pain. If you look hard enough, there are figures in the shadows---flitting, scared things, that flee from sight quicker than you can register them. But occasionally, one of them lingers, its outline rippling like smoke caught in a draft, and the weight of its anguished presence chills you to your core.

Varelli lifts his head, blinking up at you with bloodshot, distant eyes. “Are you trapped here too, children?” he murmurs, voice barely a whisper. "My sympathies... There's no escaping this place. I should know; I built these walls with my own hands..." He folds his bony hands in his lap and closes his eyes. "You’re welcome to wait here with me, if you wish. If we’re lucky---if we behave---maybe the Ladies will finally let us die…” You haven’t given up yet. But unless you find a way to convince him you’re ready to face his mistresses, Varelli’s spirit will certainly be lost to despair.
You must decide (choose one):
Release Varelli's spirit. Choose one: Search each investigator's deck and play area for the Pendant of the Antecedent and exile that card. Then, remove this card from the game. Put this card in your threat area, face down. While this card is in your threat area, the shroud of your location and all connecting locations is increased by 1.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Elio Varelli
back.subtitle: The Architect
back.flavor_text: For five centuries, Varelli built grand palaces for the Three Mothers. Now, the frail, skeletal figure you find slumped by the fireplace seems hardly aware of the world around him---discarded until his mistresses have use for him.
back.title: <unique><name>

front.text:
“Get down! We’re under fire!” Sgt. Mandel cries, cowering away from phantom mortar shells only he can see. It’s only when you hear his strangled shout---“She’s in the trees---she’s killing everyone!”---that you grasp just how deep the horror runs. Mater Suspiriorum has trapped him in his memories, and without help, he’s bound to remain a broken man in a world of invisible terrors.
You must decide (choose one):
Release Sgt. Mandel's spirit. Choose one: Search each investigator's deck and play area for Frau Perchta's Knife and exile that card. Then, remove this card from the game. Put this card in your threat area, face down. While this card is in your threat area, your base is 0.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Sgt. Frank Mandel
back.subtitle: The Plaything
back.flavor_text: Although Sgt. Mandel's physical body still languishes in a dark corner of the Arkham Sanatorium, his spirit has spent the better part of the last decade reliving the horrors of the great war for Mater Suspiriorum's amusement.
back.title: <unique><name>

front.text:
As de Castries’ spirit scribbles feverishly in his book, you leaf through some of his other recent writings, finding most have devolved into cloying, amateurish stabs at romance poetry. “I dwelt alone / In a world of moan / And my soul was a stagnant tide / Till the Lady of Darkness came to me / And stood at my side.” It is absolute drivel. There is something poetic, in a way, about the once-great writer condemned to an eternity of churning out rubbish, but you’re not so sure it's a fate he deserves.
You must decide (choose one):
Release de Castries' spirit. Choose one: Search each investigator's deck and play area for De Castries' Grand Cipher and exile that card. Then, remove this card from the game. Put this card in your threat area face down and seal the two non-symbol tokens in the chaos bag with the highest modifiers on it for the remainder of the scenario.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Thibaut de Castries
back.subtitle: The Scion
back.flavor_text:
Few in all history were as favored by Mater Tenebrarum as the writer Thibaut de Castries, whose life was one 
of fame and decadent success. And now, he is forced to demonstrate his gratitude eternally, filling page after 
page with devotions to the Mother of Darkness.
back.title: <unique><name>

front.text:
The old monk’s spirit rifles through scattered papers with trembling hands. "I don’t know," he mutters, his voice thin and reedy. "Darkness? Tears...? I thought I understood. Why can't I remember? Won’t someone help me remember?"
You must decide (choose one):
Release Brother Ross's spirit. Choose one: Search each investigator's deck and play area for Triad Figurine and exile that card. Then, remove this card from the game. Put this card in your threat area, face down. While this card is in your threat area, your base is 0.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Brother Evan Ross
back.subtitle: The Doomsayer
back.flavor_text:
Brother Ross spent his life writing about the 
mysterious nature of the Three Mothers. In their twisted gratitude, they’ve granted him just what he sought---
the opportunity to unravel all their secrets, 
and an eternity to suffer through every last one.
back.title: <unique><name>

front.text:
The meaning behind that quiet dignity soon becomes clear---frayed and worn from years of use as Mater Lachrymarum’s body, Giuliano's voice has been stolen from her. She regards you with cold and hollow eyes that implore you: leave while you still can, lest you join the endless list of the Three Mothers’ conquests. You wonder if there’s any way to free her from this eternal bondage. Something that could prove the depth of your resolve.
You must decide (choose one):
Release Ana's spirit. Choose one: Search each investigator's deck and play area for I Vespri Siciliani and exile that card. Then, remove this card from the game. Put this card in your threat area, face down. While this card is in your threat area, you must spend 1 action to play Fast cards.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Mamma Giuliano
back.subtitle: The Vessel
back.flavor_text: The real Ana Giuliano; the austere Italian woman Mater Lachrymarum wore as her host over forty years ago, not the grande dame you met at the Hotel Seasons. Even now,  bound to the Palace of Sorrows until the end of time, there's a quiet dignity to her as she endures her fate.
back.title: <unique><name>

front.text:
"Please," the old woman's spirit whispers, "I’m so tired... all this work, neverending... If I can just find my missing hand, My Lady will let me rest..." Her eyes glint with a strange gleam as she adds, "Or perhaps... you'd lend me yours? Take pity on an old soul..."
You must decide (choose one):
Release Elizabeth's spirit. Choose one: Search each investigator's deck and play area for The Hand of the Hag and exile that card. Then, remove this card from the game. Put this card in your threat area, face down. While this card is in your threat area, you have 1 fewer hand slot.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Elizabeth Salmon
back.subtitle: The Witch
back.flavor_text:
In life, Elizabeth was the proprietress of Arkham's Three Conies Inn, and a beloved daughter of Mater Tenebrarum. In death, her reward is simple: she's earned the privilege 
to toil at her mistress's feet until the end of time.
back.title: <unique><name>

front.title: <unique><name>
front.subtitle: Aradia's Vengeance
front.text:
Investigators at <name>'s location get +1 to all skill tests.
<for> At the end of the round, move <name> one location toward The Spire of Levana. Each investigator not at <name>'s location or a connecting location takes 1 horror.

That night at the Hotel Seasons, Declan had thought that the world would be at his fingertips, and Ana Giuliano would be there to enjoy it by his side. Now, he’s just another link in this chain of horrors; a ghost bound to the Palace of Sorrows. "Please," his spirit whispers, desperate to escape. "Let me go... let's make a deal, what do you say?" You're not sure what he's asking of you, but is it right to leave him here...?
You must decide (choose one):
Release O'Doyle's spirit. Choose one: Record in your campaign log that "you took Declan O'Doyle's bargain." Then, remove this card from the game. Or Put this card in your threat area, face down. While this card is in your threat area, you do not gain resources during the Upkeep phase.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Declan O'Doyle
back.subtitle: The Instigator
back.flavor_text: It’s been months, but you remember him like it was yesterday: Declan O’Doyle, the O’Bannion gang boss whose murder set off this whole, rotten mess.
back.title: <unique><name>

front.text:
"...I am pain. I am nothing but a wound. I am nothing at all..." Daria's fragile spirit sobs in anguish as she endlessly relives the pain of her death. To prevent Mater Suspiriorum from profiting further from the poor dancer's suffering, a reminder of who she truly is might pull her from this torture---or perhaps you could offer yourself up in her place, instead.
You must decide (choose one):
Release's Daria's spirit. Choose One: Search each investigator's deck and play area for the Glass Peacock and exile that card. Then, remove this card from the game. Put Daria Argent in your threat area, face down. While this card is in your threat area, your maximum health is reduced by 2.
Refuse. Tuck this card beneath the act deck and resume playing.

back.name: Daria Argent
back.subtitle: The Sacrifice
back.flavor_text:
Many talented young students lost their lives the 
night that Nussbaum Academy went up in flames. 
Daria had been the first: An offering to Mater Suspiriorum beneath Madame Pappenheimer's blade.
back.title: <unique><name>

It's difficult for you to appreciate the beauty of the 
palace's grand staircase. Instead, there's only the dread of knowing what you seek lies somewhere at its top.

"A solemn wind began to blow, the most mournful 
that ever ear heard. Mournful! That is saying nothing. 
It was a wind that had swept the fields of 
mortality for a hundred centuries.”
---Thomas De Quincey, Suspiria de Profundis

Shattered statues and crumbling effigies  
of the Sorrows' discarded identities line the 
shadowy walls of this grand hall.

Long, treacherous shadows stretch across the parlor, but the fire in the massive hearth burns like any other
---a small mercy of warmth amidst the cold elegance.

back.flavor_text:
"They wheeled in mazes; I spelled the steps. 
They telegraphed from afar; I read the signals. 
They conspired together; 
and on the mirrors of darkness my eye traced the plots."
---Thomas De Quincey, 
Levana and Our Ladies of Sorrow

back.flavor_text:
“Here were the hopes which blossom in the paths of life, reconciled with the peace which is in the grave; motions of the intellect as unwearied as the heavens, yet for all anxieties a halcyon of calm: a tranquillity that seem no product of inertia, but as if resulting from mighty and equal antagonisms; infinite activities, infinite repose.”
---Thomas De Quincey, 
Confessions of an English Opium-Eater

back.flavor_text:
From here, the sky stretches out before you---an achingly beautiful sprawl of shimmering stars adrift in a vast amethyst void, utterly unlike the storm-tossed nightmare you understood the Astral realm to be. 
But to be fair, even after all this, you still don't 
think you understand much about this place at all.

back.flavor_text:
“Rightly it is said of utter, utter misery, that it 
'cannot be remembered'; itself, being a rememberable thing, is swallowed up in its own chaos.”
---Thomas De Quincey, Suspiria de Profundis

back.flavor_text:
"There is no such thing as forgetting possible 
to the mind; just as the stars seem to withdraw 
before the common light of day... we all know that 
it is the light which is drawn over them as a veil---
and that they are waiting to be revealed."
---Thomas De Quincey, 
Confessions of an English Opium-Eater

But that's them, and not you.

Even the Sorrows have things they'd rather forget. 
This hollow void is where the things 
they deem beneath their notice are left to rot.

Shadowy figures flit through the corners of this court---
thousands upon thousands of the Sorrows' captive servants.

back.flavor_text:
“No death, no doom, no anguish can arouse the surpassing despair which flows from a loss of identity. 
Merging with nothingness is peaceful oblivion; 
but to be aware of existence and yet to know that one is 
no longer a definite being distinguished from other 
beings---that one no longer has a self---that is the 
nameless summit of agony and dread.”
---H.P. Lovecraft, Through the Gates of the Silver Key

front.flavor_text: Even now, reincarnated as a newborn goddess, Maddalena has always been blinded by her own spite. It is time to make her see.

back.name: The Old Echo Fades
back.text:
Her end is not grand. It is not regal. It is quiet. The masks orbiting her head, twisted in rage and fear. Her many eyes blink out one by one, tiny pinpricks of golden light fading into darkness. "This is mine. It was always mine! The Mothers are gone, and I… I was to be… I was supposed to be-" Her voice breaks. There’s a crack, and her body shudders as a long fissure carves itself down her center, from crown to navel. Maddalena scrambles to press the seam shut. Her eyes---all of them---shift toward you. It’s not rage anymore in her voice. It’s something far worse. Something human. "Don’t let me die like this."
R2.

front.subtitle: The Long Quiet, Forever
front.text:
<for> At the end of the round, if there is not a chaos token sealed here: Seal a random non-<auto_fail> token on <name> from the chaos bag.

<action> Spend 1 clue: Release the token sealed here, and seal a different non-<auto_fail> token on Eternal Silence.

back.flavor_text:
"She it is that night and day raves and moans, calling for vanished faces... By the power of her keys it is that Our Lady of Tears glides a ghostly intruder into the chambers of sleepless men."
---Thomas de Quincy, Suspiria de Profundis

front.flavor_text:
The interior of the Court of Sorrows begins to shift, shaping itself to suit the whims and memories of its new queen. Drunk on her newfound power, Maddalena---what remains of her---lies at the court's heart, and she has no intention of letting you leave. 
You, after all, are a loose end. And loose ends must be cut clean.

back.name: Restless Eyes
back.text:
The sound that Mater Personarum's masklike faces make isn’t a just single scream---each shriek is layered atop one another, twisted up into a single, atonal dirge. The aura around her falters, whatever sheen of divine invincibility her magic allowed her control of extinguished in an instant. She howls curses at you---defiance, fury, pride. But it’s a bluff.
Exhaust Mater Personarum and deal 1 damage to her. If Great Daemon Stolas is in the Victory Display, spawn him at Golgothan Depths, exhausted. He does not ready during the following upkeep phase.

front.flavor_text: This is how the Palace of Sorrows dies. Not by the grace of shadows, sighs, or tears, but by the primal fury of Hekate: empress of the space between spaces, mother of the line between life and death. If you do not take advantage of her mercy, this will be how you die, too.

back.name: Between the Lines
back.text: It's a true leap of faith you make when the time comes to pitch yourself through through the threshold at the center of the crossroads. There's no ground beneath you; no up, no down. Just the deafening roar of nothing pressing in on your entire being from all sides. It could be the Palace of Sorrows singing out its death throes as it's reduced to stardust and memories behind you, or the horrible, liminal sound of the void itself---it's hard to say. It's hard to think at all when it feels like every fiber of your being is about to come apart at the seams. For a moment, you're sure this is it. You're certain that you're fraying into nothing, just like Maddalena must have done. And then, finally, impact. R3.

and places where three ways meet. 
Heavenly, earthly, and in the sea, 
the saffron---cloaked goddess of graves, 
sepulchral spirit who revels with the souls of the dead."

front.flavor_text: The time to stand against the Three Mothers has come. All your preparations and planning have built to this moment. But when you replay Maddalena's swift undoing in your mind, your resolve falters---if they could do that to her, what hope do you have?

back.name: Maybe You're a Lion
back.text:
The regal weight of the Sorrows' command, the air of untouchable authority---it's begun to crack under the pressure of your perseverance. You can feel the shift in the room. Maybe their power isn’t infinite. Now, with their spells unraveled and their tempers worn raw, the truth of them is plain to see. They’re tired.
Exhaust each of the Three Mothers.

front.flavor_text:
<center>And here you stand. 
The child we once called darling. 
You, who we led astray, who we beguiled.
Ours were the symbols, yours were the words.
And now, you know elder truths, grand truths, fearful truths. 
Now, you see the things that ought not to be seen. 
And so shall our commission be finally accomplished---
that we plagued your heart until 
we have unfolded the capacities of your spirit.
How proud of you we are.</center>

back.name: Dominae Dolorosae
back.text:
Against all odds, the Three Mothers lie dying, their forms flickering like candles against the floor of the Court of Sorrows. What’s strange---what’s wrong---is the quiet grace in their defeat. "You have flown," they say, their three voices joined in unison. "When you could have broken. Persevered, when failure was all but assured. What a joy, to see our child proven within the crucible. How you do gleam." Gripped with frustration and confusion, you demand the dying witches explain themselves. After all this, all the pain they've left in their wake---they dare to feel pride? In you? But of course, there is no explanation. The Three Mothers are cryptic to the last, as they blink out of existence like dying stars, one by one. "Until next we meet."
R1.

front.flavor_text: Screams echo throughout the Hotel Seasons. You keep your head low and prepare to bolt at the first sign of a lull in the gunfire.

back.name: No Safe Passage
back.text:
You continue your tumultuous flight through the hotel corridors, but you skid to a sudden stop when you hear the sound of angry voices from around the corner. Slipping past them unnoticed will take some luck.
In player order, each investigator must test (3). Any investigator that fails this test must search the encounter deck and discard pile for a Syndicate enemy and spawn it at a connecting location. If you cannot, move the nearest Syndicate enemy to your location. It makes an immediate attack against you.

front.text: <for> Investigators cannot leave Trattoria del Parche.
front.flavor_text:
As the hour of your mysterious dinner companion's arrival draws near, you find yourself in need of a distraction. While the Trattoria del Parche's much-acclaimed floor show offers a modest reprieve from your growing boredom and anxiety, the complementary bottle of wine at your table has been a much more direct way to help ease the passage of time. 
You sneak a glance at the clock. Surely you can't be expected to wait for much longer, can you?

back.name: ...As Tardy as Too Slow
back.text:
The clock ticks on. You've nibbled through the contents of your bread basket, and while that's helped to fend off a little of the awkward feeling of waiting alone at your table, your attention remains fixed on the restaurant's entrance. You're still holding out hope that your elusive dinner companion will walk in any second now. Instead, you witness a line of trenchcoat-clad men march through the doorway, forming an ominous blockade across the front of the establishment. Against the commotion of the floor show, their arrival goes largely unnoticed. None of the other diners seem to register the moment when the men draw their firearms from beneath their coats, or when they aim squarely at the O'Bannion party. You see this all unfold before anyone else does. The grim realization of what is about to happen is yours alone. You have just enough time to flip over your table.
FlipTrattoria del Parche: La Dolce Vita over to its La Brutta Vita side. Advance to Act 1b.

front.flavor_text: All this running, and you've only managed to wind your way back to where you began. With the hotel ablaze, your only hope now to survive the evening unscathed is to cut a path through the flames to an exit---any exit.

back.name: The Escape from the Hotel Seasons
back.text:
If the act advanced at the Conservatory:
With the fire spreading quickly and the old man's corpse in relentless pursuit, there's nowhere left for you to run---not unless you make your own escape route. With all your might, you fling a nearby chair through the conservatory's glass window, and follow soon after into the night as the glass crashes down around you.
Add 1 to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. R1. If the act advanced at the Hedge Maze:
You can hear the terrible sounds of several of your fellow guests's final moments as you navigate the maze, separated from you by only a few feet of juniper. Your own demise seems like a frightening certainty, but as you turn one final corner, the hotel's driveway comes into view. You summon every last bit of your remaining strength and bolt toward the opening as fast as you can.
Add 1 to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. R1. If the act advanced at the Hotel Rooftop:
The wind on the rooftop bites at your face. Looking down, you gauge the distance to the ground below---a sizable drop, but survivable if the hedges below cushion your fall. It's not a perfect plan, but you lose the opportunity to consider any alternatives when the old man's relentless corpse emerges onto the rooftop behind you. Down has become your only viable path. You swallow your courage---and leap.
Add 1 to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. R1.

front.flavor_text: Time has become your enemy. The hatchetmen on your tail are growing closer with each passing moment.

back.name: Packing It In
back.text:
"Over there!" barks a gruff voice from behind you, followed swiftly by a din of gunfire. You've been made!
Each remaining investigator is defeated.

front.text: Try to enjoy the evening. You deserve it. (You will be instructed when to advance.)
front.flavor_text:
You can't help but steal another glance back at the table of O'Bannion men you noticed when you first entered the restaurant. The grande dame at the far end of the table departs to powder her nose, but not before leaning down to give the elderly gent at the head of the table a gentle kiss on the cheek.
Isn't it nice to see that romance is alive and well, even in these curious times?

back.name: Parting Is Such Sweet Sorrow
back.text:
The unmistakable staccato sound of gunfire erupts over your head as the restaurant descends into chaos. Glass explodes into shards around you. Stray bullets reduce the once-luxurious decor to shreds. From behind the safety of your upturned table, you can see the remnants of the O'Bannion party strewn about the floor. From what you can tell, most of them didn't even have time to react before they were gunned down in cold blood. Amidst the screams of the terrified dancers onstage, you can hear one of the hatchetmen issue a single, gruff command: "No witnesses." Your night out has been cancelled. It's time for you to go.
Put the Trattoria Kitchens and Bar L'Ammaliatrice into play, face-down. Advance to Act 2a.

front.flavor_text: A stray bullet ricochets into a porcelain vase just behind your head, shattering it into pieces. Unless you intend to finish out your evening in the back of a hearse, you need to get out of this restaurant, fast.

back.name: Out of the Frying Pan
back.text:
The Grand Ballroom is eerily silent amidst the chaos. Recognition strikes once you inspect the savaged corpse that has been propped up against the grand piano. The elderly gentleman who had been seated at the head of the O'Bannion's table now gapes up vacantly at you, his eyes gouged from their sockets and his face slashed into ribbons. If you hadn't seen him alive and well earlier tonight, you'd swear he'd been dead for weeks. Your line of thought is interrupted as the ballroom's curtains suddenly ignite, and the room erupts into flame. Panicked, you shield your eyes and stagger away from the old man's body. You push through a pair of ornate double doors, ready to resume your escape---and find yourself in back in the Tratorria del Parche's dining hall. With dismay, you realize that all you've accomplished after your terrified flight through the hotel is a single loop through the estate. There is a groan behind you. You take a glance backward into the fiery ballroom, only to see the old man's corpse rise achingly to its feet, like something out of a nightmare. The wordless hiss it makes when it notices you watching is all the encouragement you need to resume running.
Discard all enemies from play that are not currently engaged with an investigator. Move each investigator to Trattoria del Parche and return the remaining set-aside location connected to Trattoria del Parche to play, unrevealed (Bar L'Ammaliatrice or Trattoria Kitchens). Remove each revealed location other than Trattoria del Parche from the game, placing any locations with Victory X that have been cleared of clues in the victory display. Refill clues on Trattoria del Parche to its maximum clue value. Spawn the set-aside Declan O'Doyle enemy at Trattoria del Parche, exhausted. Then, shuffle the set-aside Inferno encounter set into the encounter deck, along with the encounter discard pile. Advance to Act 3a.

back.name: Tenebrarum
back.text:
The Hag tumbles backward while shielding her face from your blows, cackling with mad glee. "For God's sake, why won't she go down?" With a mad howl, the creature tumbles backward from the impact, careening into the wall with a sickening thud.
R1.

cards.name: The Haunting at the Three Conies

front.text: <for> When this agenda advances: Move all doom on it to the next agenda.
front.flavor_text: You've heard local gossip about the Three Conies for as long as you can remember. Strange occurrences have been reported in its halls ever since it was built atop the ashes of Elizabeth Salmon's razed inn, some time after she was hanged for witchcraft back in the 1840s. You can't help but wonder how the story that's unfolding now will compare.

back.name: The Shadow of Death
back.text:
Despite your efforts, your progress has been slow, and the information you've gathered is too sparse to shed light on the events unfolding within the walls of the Three Conies. Unfortunately for you, it seems that Fate has conspired to intervene---to reveal the harrowing truth behind this terrible evening.
Reveal each face-down card attached to an Apartment location. If Act 1a is the current act, remove each Crime Scene story asset not in the victory display from the game. Add 1 to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. Each investigator takes 1 horror. Shuffle the encounter discard pile back into the encounter deck. Advance the act.

front.text: Jinx -- Test (3). If you fail, resolve Miss Lila Starett's hunter keyword. If both Crime Scene cards are in the victory display: Advance.
front.flavor_text:
Finlay has successfully smuggled you inside the Three Conies, and your search for the mysterious Madame Giuliano begins. The policemen out front were looking into a string of murders that took place in the building overnight; it might be that they're connected to your own investigation.
Maybe you'll even find something the police overlooked.

back.name: The Hag of Southside
back.text:
A troubling picture emerges from the clues you've begun piecing together. The two slain men were O'Bannion associates, but the savaged, bloodied states of their rooms don't fit the bill for a typical mob hit. It's hard to imagine someone carrying out such brutal killings without alerting the other tenants. Suddenly, a horrified scream pierces the air, accompanied by a sickening crunch echoing down the corridor. You peer cautiously from behind the corner, and the ghastly sight freezes your blood in your veins. A grotesque figure that almost looks like an old woman looms over the mangled form of the building's landlady, Miss Lila. It looks up from its prey, fixes its multitude of beady eyes upon you, and darts down the hallway. It looks like you've found the murderer.
Put the set-aside The Hag enemy into play at the Third Floor. Remove Miss Lila Starett from the game. For the remainder of the scenario, whenever a scenario card refers to Miss Lila Starett: It refers to The Hag instead. Put this card next to the scenario reference card as a reminder. Reveal any remaining face-down cards attached to an Apartment location. Advance to Agenda 2a (do not resolve agenda 1b).

front.text: Jinx -- Test (3). If you fail, move Miss Lila Starett to your location. (Limit once per round.) If an effect would cause Ana Giuliano to leave The Third Floor: Cancel that effect and add 1 doom to the agenda, instead.
front.flavor_text: Chaos reignites in the aftermath of Madame Giuliano's departure, but the remaining tenants are gripped by a strange, haunting stillness---is there no way to break whatever terrible spell she has cast upon them?

back.name: The Bloodstained Butterfly
back.text:
Panic takes hold of you as you navigate the labyrinth of the Three Conies, each step more frantic than the last. The building groans under the weight of its own decay, and one misstep sends you crashing through the brittle floorboards. Your head hits something hard on the way down, leaving you dazed. As you struggle to your feet from somewhere above, you hear Madame Giuliano's imperious, taunting laughter. Dizzy and disoriented, you make a tough call: you flee before you too are claimed by Madame Giuliano's fury.
Add 1 to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. Each remaining investigator is defeated.

cards.name: The Strange Vice of Elizabeth Salmon

front.text: The Hag cannot be damaged unless she is at The Third Floor. Jinx -- Test (3). If you fail, lose 1 action.
front.flavor_text:
Whenever an occupant vanished from the Three Conies, whispers of foul play would ripple through Arkham. After all, no respectable person would dare lodge in such a place. 
But now, you have to wonder: how many of these lost souls had fallen prey to the unspeakable thing lurking within its walls?

back.name: The Bloodstained Shadow
back.text:
Desperation drives you through the building's winding halls. The building groans under the weight of its own decay, and one false step sends you crashing through the brittle floorboards. Your head hits something hard on the way down, leaving you dazed. The Hag's chilling laughter echoes closer as you struggle to your feet. Dizzy and disoriented, you make a tough call: you flee before the terrible creature can sink her fangs into you.
Add 1 to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign. Each remaining investigator is defeated.

front.text: Jinx -- Test (3). If you fail, move Miss Lila Starett to the copy of Tenement Corridors closest to you. Make sense of what is happening inside the Three Conies Apartments. At the end of the round, investigators may spend the requisite amount of clues as a group to advance.
front.flavor_text:
Gigi's horrified scream follows the sound of the landlady's gunshot. The smoking pistol slips from Miss Lila's fingers as her lifeless body hovers in midair, pulsing with a violent force that makes your eyes sting. What the hell is going on?
The sounds of gunfire and terrified screaming continue somewhere in the apartments above you. Something terrible is happening inside the Three Conies.

back.name: A Pure Formality
back.text:
The atmosphere of chaos enveloping the Three Conies seems to freeze as you meet the gaze of Ana Giuliano, the elegant grande dame from that notorious night at the Hotel Seasons. She acknowledges Gigi with a fleeting look of disinterest before turning her full attention to you. "We finally meet face-to-face. I trust your recovery has been satisfactory?" She purrs dangerously as she sizes you up. "Unfortunately, your timing couldn't be more inconvenient. I'm here to collect on a debt owed by my sister, and there are matters to settle before I can take what's mine. Clearing the building of vermin, for instance." A distant gunshot from elsewhere in the apartments punctuates her ominous statement, and Madame Giuliano takes advantage of the brief distraction to slip away behind the dilapidated door to the third floor. "Find me upstairs when you grow tired of playing games, darling. I'll be waiting for you."
Reveal The Third Floor. Gather the set-aside Vivat Regina encounter set and put Ana Giuliano into play at the Third Floor with 2 resource tokens (from the token bank) on her as barrier tokens (3, if there are 3 or more investigators.) Reveal each unrevealed location in play, along with any cards attached to them. Then, attach 1 Binding Charm treachery to each Tenant asset. Shuffle each copy of Queenly Majesty into the encounter deck, along with the encounter discard pile. Ana Giuliano's maximum barrier value is 2 (3, if there are 3 or more investigators.) Put this card next to the agenda deck as a reminder. Advance to Agenda 2c (do not resolve agenda 1b).

front.text: If a Tenant asset at your location has at least 1 clues on them: Parley. Move that asset to the victory display. The Three Conies Apartments gains ": Resign." If all Tenant story assets have been removed from the game or are in the Victory Display: Advance.
front.flavor_text: An inhuman creature lurks within Three Conies, preying upon its unsuspecting tenants. How long has this abomination resided here, and why does it choose to act now? One thing is sure: if the other residents are not warned, they may soon share poor Miss Lila's grisly fate.

back.name: Cut and Run
back.text:
With little prey left to feed upon, The Hag makes her escape. She skitters erratically down the corridor like a ricocheting bullet before crashing through the barricaded door to the third floor, shattering it into splinters. The path lies open if you dare to pursue her---assuming you're bold enough to take the risk.
Move The Hag to the Third Floor and reveal it.

front.flavor_text: Madame Giuliano's cryptic goal has become clear: she is orchestrating a dramatic purge of the Three Conies, with both her hired men and strange, unearthly forces at her beck and call. She is ready to receive you upstairs---if you are prepared for her.

back.name: Who Saw Her Die?
back.text:
In spite of all the nightmarish horrors you'd witnessed this evening, Ana Giuliano's command of the eldritch arts still manages to catch you by surprise. She swiftly counters your attacks with an imperceptible barrier, and her own barrage of withering spells inflict searing pain on you and your companions. Yet, through sheer tenacity---or a stroke of luck---you manage to gradually wear down her defenses in an intense and grueling battle. With her back to the wall, Madame Giuliano starts to laugh---a soft, self-satisfied chuckle that swells, growing louder and louder until it transforms into the howling cackle of a madwoman.
R3.

front.flavor_text: <left>Much has been written about the unique charms of San Francisco: a thrilling, near-lawless sanctuary for bohemians, intellectuals, and eccentrics. Perhaps under normal circumstances you'd relish the opportunity to explore the city by the bay, but the longer you walk its streets, the more certain you are that some unspeakable thing lies hidden deep within its heart---something that wants you gone.

back.name: The Fog, Now Risen

front.flavor_text:
"There are entities among us who are not human, perhaps not even a part of reality as we currently define it. I call them paramentals---'para' indicating 'outside' and 'elemental' being a force of nature."
<right> ---Thibaut de Castries,
 Megapolisomancy: A New Science of Cities
<left>With de Castries' seminal book in hand, you return to the streets. The murderer is out there in the fog somewhere, and you mean to find him.

back.name: A Girl and Her Dog
back.text:
You’ve begun to understand why Spadarotto was so desperate to get his hands on Thibaut de Castries' book. By tapping into the bizarre art of megapolisomancy, the art dealer has been slipping into the very fabric of the city through the fog---a trick he never imagined anyone would turn against him. When you finally find him, he’s on his hands and knees in the muck, sniveling like a dog in front of a tall, stately woman. “Miss Mercer,” he sobs, his voice thick with desperation. “Haven’t I made you proud? Isn't it enough, yet? Why aren't you happy?” Spadarotto’s tears are met with nothing but cold indifference. The fog curls around them, but it’s clear who holds the power here. Miss Mercer lifts her gaze from the pathetic sight before her to acknowledge you with a cold, mocking stare. "You big oaf," she laughs, her voice a deadly mix of sugar and ice. "All that power sure did make you stupid. You didn’t even bother to check if someone was tailing you." She turns, the sound of her heels echoing against the pavement as she walks away. “Clean up your mess.” Spadarotto whirls around, and you can see it in his eyes---he’s lost it completely. With a terrified shriek, he bolts in the opposite direction, driven by pure, mindless panic.
Move each investigator to the nearest San Francisco location and remove the following locations from the game, if applicable: Tenebrarum Lodge, Ah Toy's Pleasure Parlor, The House of Shields, and Madame Moustache's. The lead investigator must decide (choose one): We've got to stop the killer! For each Fog Token on Corona Heights, place a new Fog Token on a location in play, prioritizing locations without Fog Tokens if possible. Then, remove Corona Heights from the game. Put Pietro Spadarotto into play at the location with a fog token furthest from all investigators. Advance to Act 3a: Stop the Tenebrarum Killer! We have to follow that woman! Put Milly Mercer into play at Corona Heights. Advance to Act 3c: The Shadow of the Queen.

front.flavor_text: The headlines are the same, everywhere you look: San Francisco awakens to another gruesome murder every new day, each victim linked by a shadowy gentleman's club known as the Tenebrarum Lodge. Finding the elusive lodge's headquarters will help you learn whether Mater Tenebrarum herself is behind all of this---but first, you've got to track it down.

back.name: Inside the Black Lodge
back.text:
The chaos inside the Tenebrarum Lodge is palpable. One pale and sweating man reclines on a chaise lounge, pressing a damp cloth to a deep cut on his brow; another frantically relays information to the police over the telephone. Several lifeless bodies lie around the parlor. The wounded man opens one bloodshot eye as you make your entrance. "We've got company, Dashiell." You explain that you've been searching for the Tenebrarum Lodge, and the reclining man laughs bitterly. "Congratulations," he says, his voice laced with irony. "You've found our secret lair. Make yourself at home." The two men introduce themselves as Erle Gardner and Dashiell Hammett, two aspiring writers and members of the Tenebrarum Lodge. Once Hammett is off the phone, he gives you the lowdown: the Tenebrarum killer has struck again, just moments before your arrival. “The bastard's name is Pietro Spadarotto, an art dealer who joined the Lodge a few months back. He broke in, made a real spectacle of stealing a book, then opened fire.” You wonder aloud what book could be worth killing for. “It’s by one of our founding members: 'Megapolisomancy' by Thibaut de Castries. Some occult drivel about using geometry or buildings to do magic. Pure fiction.” Hammett shrugs, his voice tinged with disdain. “We’ve got a few copies lying around. Take one if you like. Hell, maybe it’ll even make sense to you.”
Choose an investigator to take control of the set aside Megapolisomancy story asset. Additionally, each investigator that was "invited to join the Tenebrarum Lodge" may read the following text:
You mention the invitation you received to join the Lodge, and Hammett’s expression twists into something you can’t quite pin down. "Miss Mercer doesn’t send out invitations on a whim, only to those she knows are meant for success," he says. "What did you do to impress her?" When you admit you don’t know, a slow, knowing smile curls on his lips. "I suppose it doesn’t matter," he murmurs. "If Mercer says you're in, then she must have something special in store for you."
You gain 2 experience. Search the collection for a random Humanoid or Monster weakness and add it to your deck.

front.flavor_text: You've tracked down the twisted art dealer Pietro Spadarotto, and uncovered the method behind his string of heinous murders. Now, all that's left is to cut off his escape route into the fog and put an end to his crime spree once and for all.

back.name: Just a Fling
back.text:
With nowhere for him left to run, capturing Spadarotto is surprisingly easy. The choked whine he makes when you shoulder him to the ground would be almost comical, if not for all the carnage he's left in his wake.
R1.

If an investigator at your location controls the Megapolisomancy story asset:
De Castries' book warns that the strength of Megapolisomantic magic weakens the further one ventures from a city's heart. Here, on the city’s outermost edge, you find his theory holds true---it takes far more effort than usual to bend the fog to your will. As you struggle with the mist, you catch a strange sight---a distant figure, brown and twisted, dances erratically on a faraway cliff, as if caught in the wind. You watch, uneasy, until it vanishes without a trace.

front.text:
An old woman in a fur coat steps off the trolley at Fillmore and Geary, cradling three tiny, fluffy dogs in her arms. She catches you staring and flashes you a warm smile. "I like dogs! Welcome to San Francisco,” she beams, before disappearing down the bustling city street. It strikes you as odd that she was probably the first friendly person you've met since you arrived in this awful city, and possibly the last. The trolley's conductor isn’t as cheerful. He slams a fist against the controls, cursing under his breath. "Damn thing's always breaking down," he grumbles. It looks like you won't be able to take the train for a while.

back.name: A Dish Served Cold
back.text:
Mother Helena crumples, her frail form still at last. A knot of emotions tightens in your chest---justice for the townsfolk you couldn’t save, grief for the innocents lost at Nussbaum Academy, and the raw sorrow of what you’ve just done. But that moment shatters once her lifeless body begins to convulse. Your heart skips as the corpse tears open, flesh and bone rending apart with sickening force. From the ruins of her form emerges a monstrous, winged figure drenched in Mother Helena's own blood. The thing unfurls herself, rising to her full height, towering and dreadful---a nightmare made flesh. Sister Cassandra’s scream cuts through the chamber, sharp and panicked. She stumbles backward toward the ladder, her voice trembling with horror. “No! I warned you! Now---Tisiphone comes!”

back.name: Inspector Zimmermann
back.text:

back.flavor_text:
Mild-mannered Inspector Zimmermann has served the 
Freiburg Police force faithfully for nearly twenty years. He's spent ten of those years as a faithful thrall of the Mother of Sighs.

front.text: Jinx -- Choose one: (Limit once per round.) Take 1 horror. Take 1 damage. Draw the top card of the encounter deck. Find what you came here for. You will be instructed when to advance.
front.flavor_text: You find yourself in the Abbey of St. Walpurga, somewhere deep in the Black Forest. You're closer than ever to finding Mater Suspiriorum, but it's clearer than ever that whatever's waiting for you at journey's end will not be easy or pleasant.

back.name: Helena
back.text: The ladder creaks under your weight as you descend into the chamber beneath the anchoress’ cell, and a fetid stench hits you like a blow. A cavern of bones and decay stretches before you. On one side, the missing townsfolk sit huddled, silent, shaking with fear. On the other, an old nun sits with her back to you, her frail frame facing the damp stone wall. From above, a frantic voice breaks the oppressive quiet. “Please, don’t hurt her!” A young nun scrambles down after you, her eyes wide with desperation. She stumbles over her words, tears streaking her face. “I'm Sister Cassandra. Mother Helena has served this Abbey for years, taking away the suffering of all who came seeking solace. But tonight...” Her voice cracks. “Tonight, whatever divine grace filled her is gone. She doesn’t hear us, doesn’t see us---doesn’t feel anything. She’s been abandoned. Can’t you see?” The old nun doesn’t stir, even as you approach. Her body doesn’t flinch under your scrutiny. Either Sister Cassandra and Mother Helena are talented actresses both, or the truth is even more pitiful: this woman is now an empty shell. “Please,” Sister Cassandra pleads, her voice raw. “Take the townsfolk and go. She may be hollow, but I can’t abandon her too---not after all she’s done for us. I owe her that much.”

cards.name: The Other Side of the World

front.text: Jinx -- Put 1 clue on The Midwife's Tunnel from the token bank. If "you opened the path," Advance.
front.flavor_text: By the time you reach the Schauinsland, the twilight sky has turned dark. You're here chasing rumors about an old tunnel that connects the two neighboring villages on either side of the mountain---and perhaps to the missing townsfolk, as well. But now that you're here, trudging through damp, thick clumps of fresh snowfall, you'll be lucky if you can even find your footing.

front.flavor_text: The hidden path inside the Midwife's Tunnel spills out into a cavern so vast, it makes you forget the frozen wasteland outside. Everything’s green as far as the eye can see; a secret world locked beneath the winter frost. Someone’s been through here recently, that much is clear from the lit torches that line the stone path forward. But as for what---or who---you’ll find at its end, that’s anyone’s guess.

back.name: Walpurga's Road
back.text:
Around the base of the brazier lie small square stones inscribed with writing, each no larger than a notebook page. Some of the languages are indecipherable, but you identify others---English, Chinese, Latin. On inspection, it becomes obvious what the writing on these stones is: they're countless names. Zorya Utrennyaya. Su Daji. Delphine LaLaurie. Caterina Maria de' Medici. Dorothea Spitznagel. Helena Nussbaum. Thousands of them, each etched into their own stone.
The investigator who flipped over Mother's Cradle must immediately add the set-aside Katadesmos of Anima weakness to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator's deck size.
The second your eyes pass over Helena Nussbaum's name, the stone slab at the far end of the clearing groans and grinds backward to reveal yet another dark, hidden pathway. You take a breath, but it’s already too late to turn back. You step inside. After what feels like hours of trudging down the dark tunnel, a wooden hatch in the ceiling above blocks your path, its slats letting in thin streams of pale moonlight. You reach up, and with a soft creak, the hatch swings open with surprising ease. You rise up into a small courtyard: neat, quiet, and still. A vegetable garden sits off to one side; on the other, the shadow of a chapel steeple looms over the courtyard wall. You’ve surfaced inside a small abbey somewhere in the Black Forest---but why?
Remove all doom from Agenda 1a. Each investigator loses all of their clues. Put each Convent location into play. Proceed to Interlude: The Abbey of St. Walpurga.

front.flavor_text: You've discovered the entrance to a twisting maze of tunnels and crypts under the Haus zum Walfisch. If the missing townspeople were spirited away through these catacombs, you have to wonder---what terrible purpose lay in wait for them, so far beneath the city?

You’ve travelled all the way to Germany, chasing after the shadow of Mater Suspiriorum: the eldest of the Three Mothers, shepherd of the despairing and forgotten. Can you find her before more of Freiburg’s broken souls take her hand and vanish into the dark? 
Or will you be the next to slip away?

back.name: In Silent Communion
back.text:
The church bell at Freiburg Munster tolls, its deep chime cutting through the cold, misty air. Somewhere in an old, ancient abbey deep in the Black Forest, the last desperate cries of the missing townsfolk fade into silence.
You've run out of time. Each remaining investigator is defeated.

front.subtitle: The City in the Black Forest
front.text: <action> Choose and discard a non-weakness card from your hand: Draw 2 cards. (Limit once per round.)
front.flavor_text:
As night falls, you can feel the city buzz with 
a curious energy, as if something unspeakable 
lies just behind its fairytale veneer.

back.flavor_text:
The city's streets awash in the aroma of 
roasted chestnuts from market stalls and the 
earthy fragrance of centuries-old timber. 
The locals say the coming winter will be a cold one.

front.text:
It turns out you're not the only ones searching for the missing townsfolk. Near the student dormitories, you're intercepted by a young, earnest police inspector named Fritz Vogel. He’s almost too eager to question you, and your conversation quickly shifts to comparing notes. “It was late, you know?" Vogel says, recounting a young man he tailed earlier that week before he disappeared into thin air. There was something strange in the way the boy moved---like he wasn’t really there anymore, just... following something. Figured he was a drunk. Last I saw him was near the Münsterplatz. Then, gone. Vanished." Before Vogel excuses himself, he leaves an offer to meet again should your search bear any fruit. "If you find anything, let me know. If I’m off duty, Inspector Hans Zimmermann’s the man posted here. I'm sure he'll be keen to help you out."
Choose an investigator at your location to test or (2). If that test succeeds, remove X clues from The Cathedral of Our Lady and return them to the token bank. X is the amount the test succeeded by (to a minimum of 1.)
Flip this card back over and put 1 clue on University of Freiburg from the token bank. This card may be flipped over again.

front.flavor_text:
Albert-Ludwigs University of Freiburg is the fifth-oldest university in all of Germany, and the first to accept 
female students. Its student dormitories are currently kept under strict curfew, given the recent disappearances.

front.flavor_text: Built in the 16th century, The Whale House famously served as a refuge to the philosopher Erasmus as he fled the Reformation. Today, the historic building lies vacant.

front.subtitle: Freiburg Münster
front.text: : Parley. Heal 1 horror and draw a card.
front.flavor_text:
Evening Mass is just getting underway. Maybe there’s something in today's sermon that’ll steel your nerves 
for the night ahead, if you happen to be a believer. 
If not, at least it’s warm inside.

back.flavor_text: Once called the most beautiful spire on God's Earth, Freiburg Münster looms majestically above the cityscape.

front.text:
It takes a while for it to click---why the Whale House feels so wrong whenever you pass it by. The stonework is older, weathered by time and neglect, but there's no mistaking it. The place is almost identical to Nussbaum Academy. The resemblance is too close to be a coincidence. Once you decide to break inside, your suspicions deepen. The layout is the same---Every hall, every corner. It's like you're walking through the same nightmare all over again. Following a hunch, you head for where the headmistress’s office would have been, and find exactly what you were looking for: a secret passage, in the exact same place you found it back at the Academy.
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Put each Catacomb location into play and shuffle the set-aside Paranormal Activity encounter set into the encounter deck, along with the encounter discard pile. Remove all doom from Agenda 1a.
Remember that "you have found the way forward." Flip this card back over. It may not be flipped over again.

If the investigators possess fewer than 3 clues:
You stare into flames of the pyre in the middle of the clearing, waiting for... what, exactly? Something. Anything? You're starting to feel a little ridiculous.
Flip this card back over and put 1 clue on Mother's Cradle from the token bank. This card may be flipped over again.
If the investigators possess 3 or more clues:
The flickering light from the pyre in the center of the clearing casts long shadows across the the earth. Your foot catches on something solid, obscured by the darkness---a half-buried root? You glance down, and you nearly leap back in shock. It's not a root, but the jagged remains of a human jawbone. The rest of the skull is still attached, half-submerged in the dusty earth, skeletal hands clawing upward like a swimmer lost beneath the surface. Before you can fully process the horror, you spot another one just a few yards away. And another. And another---dozens, no, hundreds of skeletons lie scattered across the clearing, half-buried in the mossy ground around the flame.
The investigators must spend 3 clues, as a group. Remember that "you unearthed a secret." Flip this card back over. It may not be flipped over again.
