A pyre burns at the center of the stone circle, 
sending tendrils of smoke coiling upward into the cavern's ceiling.

front.subtitle: The Hexenweg
front.text:
Jinxed.
<for> When you attempt to leave <name>, if there are any clues remaining on it: Test <willpower> or <agility> (3). If you fail, flip this card over and resolve the text on its other side.
front.flavor_text:
A long stone path stretches out toward a grassy hillside, 
across a still body of water. It's hard to believe this calm green sanctuary exists beneath the Schauinsland.

front.text:
In the center of the disk, a massive tree rises from the earth. On the disc's outer ring, a city rises from the ground---wattled huts stand aside structures shockingly similar to the Bavarian tinder-framed buildings found throughout Freiburg, behind which rise a series of tall, gray towers studded with empty windows. A lone bird flies between the city and a bleak expanse littered with supine stick figures, strewn like fallen leaves. And there, at the other end of the outer ring, stands a featureless gray figure with three heads, its right arm raised in salutation. Something about the figure feels wrong, almost threatening, threatening, and the longer you stare at it, the more your discomfort grows. It is then that you see it: the small stone carving at the base of the giant disc. It's almost identical to the figure.
Test (3). If you fail, take 1 mental trauma.
Whether you succeeded or failed at the test above, choose an investigator to put the set-aside Triad Figurine into their hand. That investigator may choose to add it to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator's deck size.

It's hard to tell where the sounds are coming from, but you’re almost sure you heard someone whisper your own name. You glance around the cavern, checking to see if you've been followed. Nothing. Not a living soul in sight---until your eyes land on a raven, perched on a nearby rock, busy picking apart the remains of an unlucky rat. Its beak works with a grim efficiency. And then, as if sensing your gaze, the bird's cold, black eyes meet yours. Without warning, it lets out a sharp cry and swoops straight at you.
Search the encounter deck and discard pile for a Weeping Familiar enemy and draw it.
Flip this card back over. This card may be flipped over again.

Veiled. Jinxed.
<reaction> When you investigate this location, increase the shroud of <name> by 2 for this attempt: Look at the top card of either the encounter deck or any player deck. You may choose to put that card on the bottom of its deck.
front.flavor_text:
At the base of the verdant island lies a massive stone disc, 
twenty-five feet tall and covered in crude, childlike paintings.

front.subtitle: Berghotel Schauinsland
front.text:
Veiled.
<free> Spend 1 resource: Search the top 3 cards of your deck for an asset and draw it. If a weakness is discovered among the searched cards, draw it as well. (Limit once per investigator.)
front.flavor_text: Zur Friedrichsruhe was originally built in the 19th century by the stage manager of Theater Freiburg. Appropriately, it's quite a dramatic sight against the backdrop of the Schauinsland's peak.

front.text:
Heinrich Blumhoff, the head of staff at the Berghotel Schauinsland, frowns as you lay out your reason for coming up the mountain. "The old Midwife’s Tunnel? Locked up tight, I’m afraid. Too many young folks causing trouble---the vandalizing, drawing the rude pictures on the walls, the sneaking off to… misbehave... It’s bad for business, you understand." Well. If Herr Blumhoff’s worried about his bottom line, you’ve got a pretty good idea how to grease his wheels...
Investigators at Zur Freidrichsruhe may choose to spend any combination of 4 resources or clues.
If you chose to spend the required amount of resources and/or clues: Ignore the forced text on The Midwife's Tunnel for the remainder of the game. (Place a horror token on The Midwife's Tunnel as a reminder.) Flip this card back over. This card may be flipped over again.
Otherwise, flip this card back over and put 1 clue on Zur Freidrichsruhe from the token bank. This card may be flipped over again.

You walk the length of the Midwife’s Tunnel twice over without finding a thing, but it's on your third pass that something truly odd occurs. A tall figure approaches you from down the long, dark tunnel, its hidden face behind a shaggy, grotesque mask. “You must decide now,” the thing rasps as you draw closer. “Turn back, and you may never reach this place again. Continue, and you may be lost.” You’re too stunned to respond, your words lost somewhere between disbelief and dread. The masked figure sniffs the air like a bloodhound before it resumes its slow, deliberate pace past you and down the Midwife's Tunnel. Just before it vanishes into the gloom, it offers you one final piece of advice over its shoulder: “You must not shed blood in the garden. You are warned.” The encounter is over in less than a minute. As the strange figure disappears from sight, a sudden gust of wind whips through the tunnel. And then---where there was only solid rock before---a new path into the darkness lies behind you, a mouth yawning open in the stone.
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Put each Hexenweg location into play and shuffle the set-aside Agents of Tears encounter set into the encounter deck, along with the encounter discard pile. Remove all doom from Agenda 1a.
Remember that "you opened the path." Flip this card back over. It may not be flipped over again.

front.flavor_text:
This tunnel was built to allow for passage 
between the hamlets of Kappler and Hofsgrund 
on either side of the mountain. It's been 
sealed up tight for the past several years.

front.text:

Skill cards have 1 additional <wild> symbol when committed to tests at this location.
front.flavor_text:
From the heights of the Schauinsland, 
Freiburg looks like a tiny toy city nestled amongst the trees.

front.text:
Veiled.
<for> After successfully investigating <name>, test <willpower> or <intellect> (3). If you fail, you must immediately move to a connecting location.
front.flavor_text:
Almost all the walls of this old monastery 
have crumbled to dust. What little remains behind 
has all but been reclaimed by the forest.

front.text:
If the investigators possess fewer than 3 clues:
You pull yourself out of the dense treeline, only to arrive at the ruins of the old chapel for the fourth---no, fifth time. You're going in circles.
Flip this card back over and put 1 clue on Forsaken Chantry from the token bank. This card may be flipped over again.
If the investigators possess 3 or more clues:
You trace your fingers along the weathered stone, brushing centuries of dirt from the inscription on the chapel's crumbling outer wall. The carved stone reveals a single Latin word carved into the stone: "Silentium." Inside the dilapidated old church, you crouch down to brush away debris from the base of where the altar must have once stood, and there it is: a faint seam in the stone, hidden in plain sight. With a soft groan, the passage opens, revealing a stairway spiraling down into darkness.
The investigators must spend 3 clues, as a group. Remember that "you unearthed a secret." Flip this card back over. It may not be flipped over again.

Movement flickers at the edges of your vision---hazy, indistinct shadows that slip through the trees. Whatever they are, they don’t approach, instead merely lingering on the periphery of your vision. There must be a dozen of them, maybe more, but in the dim light it's impossible to tell for sure.
Search the encounter deck and discard pile for a copy of Grasping Shadow and spawn it at a connecting location. Flip this card back over. This card may be flipped over again.

<action>: Exile a single card in your deck worth a minimum of 3 experience. Defeat the Schrätelhexe. (Limit once per scenario.)
front.flavor_text:
It looks like folks have been leaving offerings in this 
shadowy thicket for ages---trinkets, tokens. Little gifts.
You could leave something of your own, if you'd like.

front.text:
It’s deep within the thicket, nestled among the gnarled trees and tangled vines, that you find the first of the statues. The figure is life-sized and carved from a pale gray marble with an odd, slick texture. The subject, a young woman in a flapper's dress, seems frozen in terror. Around a tree, another statue awaits---a young man in policeman’s garb, his hand half-raised in some futile gesture of defense. And deeper still, you find another---a little girl, barely ten, her body contorted as if caught in mid-scream. Are these merely statues? Or were these victims of the Schrätelhexe---or something worse? Something by the little girl's feet glints in the faint light. You stoop to claim it.
Test (3). If you fail, take 1 mental trauma.
Whether you succeeded or failed at the test above, choose an investigator to put the set-aside Frau Perchta's Knife into their hand. That investigator may choose to add it to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator's deck size.

Jinxed.
<for> If you fail an fight, evade or parley action at this location: Flip this card over. (Limit once per round.)
front.flavor_text:
The Bannwalds---"Protected Woods"---used to be where 
princes and dukes claimed parts of the forest as their personal hunting grounds. But Bannwald Feldberg earned its name 
for another reason: everyone knows these woods are bewitched.

front.subtitle: Zie Ravennaschlucht
front.text:
Veiled. Jinxed.
<name> gets +1 shroud for each clue below its maximum clue threshold.
As an additional cost to take a move action at <name>, spend 1 additional action.
front.flavor_text:
The gentle sound of rushing water at the bottom of the 
gorge is certainly pleasant, but ultimately does very little to 
make navigating the cramped thicket less frustrating.

front.text:
Thick roots and thorned bushes crowd the path at the bottom of the gorge. Somewhere far ahead of you, a figure moves---just out of reach. She slips between the trees, but not before you catch a glimpse. Could it be? She matches the description of one of the missing young women from the city. But as you round a bend in the gorge, your excitement over finding the missing girl curdles into horror. There, sprawled in the mud by the creekside, lies a skeleton. The tattered clothing draped across its bones bears an uncanny resemblance to what the missing woman had been last seen wearing. But the body---it’s wrong. The decay, the way the flesh has all but rotted away, is far more advanced than the mere days she’s been gone. It shouldn’t be possible. Before you can investigate further, the last sliver of sunlight vanishes, swallowed by the canopy overhead. In an instant, the gorge plunges into total darkness. And then, the horrible, cackling laughter begins.
Each investigator loses all of their clues. Put each Bannwald location into play and shuffle the set-aside Trauma encounter set into the encounter deck, along with the encounter discard pile. Remove all doom from Agenda 1a.
Remember that "you made a troubling discovery." Flip this card back over. It may not be flipped over again.

front.subtitle: Silva Marciana
front.text: <reaction> After you enter <name> from another <t>Schwarzwald</t> location, test <willpower> (X). X is the number of cards in your hand. If you succeed, take an immediate move action.
front.flavor_text:
There are answers to your questions, 
somewhere deep in these dark woods.

front.text:
The wind picks up across the lake, carrying with it a sound: your name, whispered so faintly you almost think you imagined it. You turn instinctively, to answer the call--- And you’re home. Your childhood home. You can hear your family in the next room, chatting happily among themselves. Everything is just as you remember it, down to the smallest detail---even the smell. Emotion floods over you like a tidal wave. You run, eager to explore, to touch each familiar corner. But as you rush to start revisiting this impossible place, you pitch forward. You’ve fallen waist-deep in the icy waters of Lake Titisee, your legs sinking into the muddy depths as you stop yourself from walking toward the center of the lake. Was that a memory? Who called your name? What do you think you're doing?
Take 1 horror. You may choose to take 1 more horror. For each horror you took (to a maximum of 2), you may move a clue from a connecting location to Lake Titisee. Flip this card over. This card may be flipped over again.

Jinxed. Veiled.
<for> After you move to <name>: You cannot discover more than 1 clue at this or any connecting location until the end of the round.
front.flavor_text:
As you trudge along the shore, a biting wind begins 
to pick up from the far side of the lake.

front.text:

front.flavor_text: Rows of coffins line the inside of this long, dark chamber.

front.text:

front.flavor_text:
How many people had to pass on, 
just for their remains to end up in this single room?

front.text:
As you push deeper into the winding, subterranean passages beneath Freiburg, the sounds of the city above are replaced with something altogether different---the sound of quiet whispers, too faint to understand. You had thought that you were just been hearing snippets of conversations from the town above, but as the minutes drag on, you start to see them---the silvery figures, flickering at the edge of your vision. Men, women, and children, moving like shadows in the desolate corners of the tunnels. You're trespassing in the realm of Freiburg's dead.
Test (3). If you fail, search the encounter deck and discard pile for a copy of Hateful Apparition and draw it.
Flip this card back over. This card may be flipped over again.

You've pushed, prodded, and even prayed at the shrine, all to no avail. You've begun to feel a little foolish. It's only after exhausting your options that you notice the An inscription, faint and worn, etched intoe base of the shrine. You lean closer to make out the words, written in German: "Hier liegen die Überreste von Elio Varelli; Architekt des Haus zum Walfisch und lebenslanger Freund von Erasmus." "Here lie the remains of Elio Varelli; Architect of the Whale House and lifelong friend of Erasmus." Elio Varelli? Could he be related to the man who built the Hotel Seasons in Arkham? That would be a strange coincidence, indeed. Before you can make sense of it, a soft, metallic clink breaks the silence. A small object has fallen from the shrine. You kneel, fingers brushing the cold ground, and reach for it.
Choose an investigator to put the set-aside Pendant of the Antecedent into their hand. That investigator may choose to add it to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator's deck size.

Your search through the crypt yields little more than dust, until you find the sarcophagus belonging to Dorothea Spitznagel: Mother Superior of the order of St. Walpurga. You frown. Why would a nun be entombed here beneath the streets of Freiburg, rather than on consecrated ground? Especially a nun of such importance? On a hunch, you grip the edge of the heavy lid and push. The stone groans in protest, but eventually shifts. Instead of the withered remains of a centuries-dead nun, you find something far stranger: a set of stone steps, spiraling down into deeper darkness...
The investigators must spend 3 clues, as a group. Remember that "you unearthed a secret." Flip this card back over. It may not be flipped over again.

## When Man first began to dream,

they were there to plague Him.

When the last Man on Earth dies,

they will be there to mourn Him.

<center>*"Banish the frailties of hope, wither the relenting of love, scorch the

fountain of tears, curse him as only thou canst curse. So shall he be

accomplished in the furnace, so shall he see the things that ought not to be

seen, sights that are abominable, and secrets that are unutterable."*

<center>       ---Thomas De Quincy, *Levana and Our Ladies of Sorrow*

<left>***Night of Vespers*** is an original fan campaign for *Arkham Horror: The Card Game* for 1--4 players, inspired by Thomas De Quincy's *Suspiria De Profundis*, Dario Argento's* Le Tri Madri* film trilogy, and Miskatonic River Press's* Our Ladies of Sorrow* by Kevin Ross. ***Night of Vespers*** contains eight scenarios,* each of which may also be played on their own in Standalone Mode.

## Additional Rules and Clarifications

<Header>New Keywords: Jinx & Jinxed</header>

<bullet><hsp> <left>Investigators will encounter the pervasive and unpredictable effects of

ancient witchcraft throughout the Night of Vespers campaign in the

form of the **Jinx and Jinxed** keywords.

<bullet><thsp> **When an investigator fails a fight, evade, or investigate test when

<hsp> a card with the jinxed keyword is at their location, players at that

<hsp> location must refer to the current act or agenda and resolve the

<hsp> forced effect connected to the bolded **Jinx** text. **

<bullet> **Example:** *During the mythos phase, **Sebastian Benitez** draws

a treachery that enters play at his location with the jinxed

keyword. During the following investigation phase, he takes an Investigate

action at that location and fails. The current agenda features the text

"**Jinx --** Increase the shroud of your location by 1 until the end of the

round.**" Because Sebastian failed an investigate test while the treachery

with the jinxed keyword was in play at his location, his location's shroud

is increased by 1 until the end of the round. *

<bullet><hsp> If a card with the jinxed keyword enters play but its effects are not

defined by either the current act or agenda, **failed fight, evade, or

investigate tests do not trigger the jinxed keyword.**

<bullet> **Example:** *An enemy with the jinxed keyword enters **Elsie

Malone'**s location and engages her. Neither the current act or agenda

define any specific ruling for the jinxed keyword; therefore, if Elsie fails a

fight or evade test against this enemy, it will not trigger any additional

effects.*

<bullet><thsp> **The effects of multiple Jinxed cards in play at the same location are

<hsp> not cumulative unless otherwise specified.**

<bullet>** Example: *Simone Toussaint** is engaged with 2 enemies with the Jinxed

keyword. The current act has the text **Jinx -- Increase the difficulty of

all tests at this card's location by 1 until the end of the round.** If

Simone fails a fight test against one of those enemies, the difficulty of all

tests performed at her location are increased by **1 until the end of the

round, and not 2.** *

## Campaign Setup

To set up the *Night of Vespers* campaign, perform the following steps in order.

**1. Choose investigator(s).

2. Each player assembles their investigator deck.

3. Choose difficulty level.

4. Assemble the campaign chaos bag.**

<bullet> **Easy (A Pleasant Evening):**

+1, 0, 0, –1, –1, –2, –2, –3, <skull>, <skull>, <skull>, <elder_sign>, <auto_fail>.

<bullet> **Standard (A Night on the Town):**

+1, 0, –1, –1, –2, –2, –2, –3, –3, –4, <skull>, <skull>, <tablet>, <cultist>, <elder_sign>, <auto_fail>

<bullet> **Hard (A Night to Remember):**

0, 0, –1, –2, –2, –3, –3, –4, –5, <skull>, <skull>, <tablet>, <cultist>, <elder_thing>, <elder_sign>, <auto_fail>

<bullet> **Expert (A Night to Forget):**

0, –1, –2, –3, –3, –4, –4, –5, –6, <skull>, <skull>, <tablet>, <cultist>, <elder_thing>, <elder_sign>, <auto_fail>

**You are now ready to begin at the Prologue.**

sections.name: p3
sections.markdown:
## Prologue

**Prologue:** * You find the envelope placed strategically atop your daily clutter. Someone clearly intended for you to find it. There was no chance you wouldn't have noticed it throughout the routine of your day; no chance you'd ignore something so unusual.

You flip the small thing back and forth in your hand, appreciating the weight of it against your fingers. You've yet to solve the puzzle of who might have left it for you, but the delicate blend of woodsmoke and lavender that scents the paper does much to pique your curiosity. With a touch of excitement, you break open the nondescript wax seal of the envelope and begin to read the handwritten message addressed to you within.

<center><family "Pristina"><size 11.0>*Join me for a lovely Italian dinner at Trattoria del Parche.

Hotel Seasons.

8:00 P.M., the evening of September 10th.

No questions. Don't be late. Dress your best.

It will be worth it.*</size></family>

<left>The message provides no clues about its sender, but that only adds to the growing sense of mystique. Ever since the Varelli family mansion was reinvented as the Hotel Seasons last year, it has swiftly risen to become a jewel among Massachusetts' finest destination hotels. If your mysterious host has chosen the glamorous hotel for your eventual meeting, you're certain to be in for quite a captivating evening.

Today is September the 9th. You have just enough time to find something to wear.*

<right>Proceed to **Scenario 1: The End of Seasons.**

## Scenario 1: The End of Seasons

**Intro 1:** *Fifteen years ago, renowned Italian architect Signor Elio Varelli made his way to Arkham with a mind to construct a palatial estate in which to live out his twilight years. When Varelli passed unexpectedly shortly after the mansion's completion, its ostentatious splendor fell into almost immediate disrepair. What should have been a masterpiece estate from one of Europe's finest architects very quickly became a colossal, sagging eyesore at the top of French Hill.

Reborn this year as the Hotel Seasons, the estate extends now a warm invitation to travelers along the Eastern Seaboard, promising luxury beyond compare. When you enter the hotel's lobby and take in the luxurious shades of its red and gold decor, you find that the establishment looks very much like the palace that Varelli had always meant it to be. The hotel's concierge efficiently verifies your reservations and offers a gracious escort to its ground-floor restaurant, the Trattoria del Parche. He says nothing about the identity of your mysterious dinner companion, and merely encourages you to enjoy the floor show until they make themselves known.*

*Inside, the restaurant is alive with activity. A dance troupe pirouettes on a nearby stage; a graceful performance for an audience that appears much more interested in their own food. The buzz of conversation dominates the atmosphere, the loudest of which comes from a rowdy party of diners seated nearby.

Ten rough-faced diners crowd around the nearby table, their voices raised as they engage in drunken one-upmanship. Seated at the table's head is an elderly couple, elegantly attired---but clearly inebriated. You've been in Arkham long enough to recognize the O'Bannion gang when you see them.*

:::standalone

<bullet> If any investigators in the campaign have the ***Criminal, Detective, Police***, or ***Reporter*** traits, choose one of those players to read the following passage out loud. Otherwise, skip to **Intro 2.**

*The elderly man at the head of the table is no stranger to you. Declan O'Doyle is an enforcer for the O'Bannion gang, notorious for his efficiency and ruthlessness. You've heard rumors for months about a rift forming between him and Naomi O'Bannion, the gang's de facto leader, but from where you're sitting Declan looks like he's doing just fine. You don't recognize his companion, the older woman at his side with an aura of quiet gravitas. The way she carries herself suggests she's every bit as formidable as Declan is.*

<bullet> You begin this scenario with 1<investigator> clues from the token bank.

:::

<right>Proceed to **Intro 2.**

<left>**Intro 2:** *Before you can entertain that train of thought any further, the

Maître d' bustles over to your table to make a fuss about taking your drink orders. Once he shuffles away, you are finally left to settle into your seat.

You realize that you're a little nervous. The anticipation of your mysterious companion's arrival continues to build with each passing moment, and it's hard not to wonder just what kind of excitement the rest of your evening will hold in store.*

<right> Proceed to **Setup.**

:::image-bottom
./images/quentin-bouilloud-main.jpg
:::

sections.name: p5
sections.markdown:
:::resolution

**If no resolution was reached because each investigator was defeated:** *The dissonant sounds of gunfire and screaming overwhelm your senses. There is a single, terrible moment when you attempt to flee and are caught in the sudden crossfire. A stray bullet strikes your shoulder. The sudden jolt of pain is almost unbearable, but you grit your teeth and press onward, until in a moment of genius---or sheer desperation---you dive into a utility closet, brace yourself against the door, and begin to apply pressure to your wound with a discarded dish towel. There's only so much you can do to stop the bleeding with a rag, but the relief you feel from escaping your assailants is a fair substitute for anesthesia.

Several hours later, it's in that very utility closet that the authorities discover you---disoriented, pain-stricken, and covered in your own blood. You're gingerly placed onto a stretcher, whisked away to the safety of St. Mary's Hospital, where skilled hands tend to your injuries. As for the events of that night---your front row seat to the ambush on the O'Bannions' by a rival gang, the puzzling benefactor who lured you in to witness the bloody event, and the tangled riddle of your own misfortune---your memories are hazy, and the full story may be ever beyond your grasp. But you're alive, and still in one piece. That has to count for something.*

<bullet><hsp> Each investigator receives 1 physical trauma.

<bullet><hsp> In your campaign log, record that *you were shot at the

Hotel Seasons.*

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to **Resolution 2.**

**Resolution 1:** *The city of Arkham hasn't needed to contend with the same level of crime as nearby Boston, but it's certainly no stranger to gangland violence. In any other circumstance, the attack on the O'Bannion party by a rival syndicate would be a textbook tragedy---a terrible shame, but one well within the bounds of belief. But when your evening takes a detour into the bizarre as the eyeless corpse of Declan O'Doyle starts shambling after you in relentless pursuit, you're forced to concede that this evening is anything but ordinary. Once you pull yourself to your feet, you manage to limp haphazardly down the hotel's driveway just as a distant wail of sirens finally announces the late arrival of the Arkham police department. The rush of adrenaline that fueled your escape finally fades, and you collapse to your knees just as the authorities manage to clamber out of their squad cars.

:::resolution

*You're exhausted and bloody, and the police quickly find that you're in no shape to answer their many questions. You're swiftly placed on a stretcher and whisked away in the back of an ambulance bound for St. Mary's hospital. Any answers that you had hoped would explain the unsettling turn of events your evening has taken are going to have to wait.*

<bullet><hsp> In your campaign log, record that *you escaped the Hotel Seasons.*

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to **Resolution 2.**

**Resolution 2:** *You are forced to spend the next week convalescing in your hospital bed. Thanks to the Arkham Gazette's exhaustive coverage and an unfriendly grilling by a couple of detectives from the Arkham Police Department, you've begun piecing together the puzzle of what truly happened that night. The Hotel Seasons now lies in ruins, devoured by flames that the Arkham Gazette seems content to blame on faulty wiring. However, the real meat of the newspaper's coverage is the raging turf war between Boston's Italian Syndicate and the O'Bannion Gang that has taken over the city. It seems that Declan O'Doyle, the old man at the center of the night's events, had been courting the syndicate behind the O'Bannions' backs for some time. His very public demise at the Hotel Seasons was a loud and clear message to Naomi and her men: the Italians have no taste for traitors, signalling that business between the two outfits had come to a close. Their new aim? To stamp out the Irish gang once and for all, wresting control of Arkham's underground from their fingers. The Arkham Police Department has called in backup from Boston, but until those reinforcements arrive, the gang war won't be easing up anytime soon.

You still don't know why you were called to the Trattoria del Parche that evening, or the identity of the person whose invitation allowed you a front row seat to the carnage. It's not until you are ready to be discharged from the hospital that you find that someone has left something for you at the hospital's front desk. This time, there's a catch: there are two messages for you, and each one claims to be sent from your mysterious benefactor.*

<bullet><hsp> Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.

<bullet><hsp> The time you've spent recovering at St. Mary's Hospital has allowed you the opportunity to lick your wounds. Each investigator may choose to heal 1 mental or physical trauma. Each investigator who chooses to do so must search the collection for a random basic <t>Flaw</t> or <t>Injury</t> weakness and add it to their deck. This card does not count toward their deck size.

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to **Interlude: Two Messages.**

:::image-bottom
./images/hayo-koekkoek-hc-lobby-c.jpg
:::

sections.name: p6
sections.markdown:
## Interlude I: Two Messages

**Interlude 1:***Your cab ride home is a silent affair. Though the two telegrams you hold in your hands both seem to know you were at the Trattoria del Parcae the night of the O'Bannion job, their tones couldn't be more different from one another. It's clear to you that at least one of them---perhaps both of them---can't be from your original benefactor.*

<bullet><hsp> Read over the two telegrams in the boxes below, then proceed to

**Interlude 2.**

:::story

**Telegram 1:** *The first message was sent only a day after events unfolded at the Hotel Seasons, written in an uneven hand that is markedly different from the delicate script your original invitation had been penned in. It reads:

<center><family "Ink Free">Still more to discuss---the worst is yet to come.

Meet Sept 18, Cavalier Speakeasy---Southside.

Have the answers you need.

Password: Tullamore.

---F.

:::

:::story

**Telegram 2:*** The second message arrived several days into your stay at St. Mary's. It is professionally typed, and its postmark reveals that it was sent from Boston.

<center><family "High Tower Text">Request your presence at the Parker House Hotel

in Boston on the evening of Sept 18

Please accept apologies for the continued mystery

Importance cannot be understated

Happy you made it out in one piece

---GG

:::

**Interlude 2:*** You mull the two messages over. Your curiosity demands answers, but there's no telling who or what is waiting for you at either destination. Either one of these telegrams could end up spelling trouble for you, and you'll only be able to choose one of them to attend. Hopefully, it'll be the right one.*

<bullet><hsp> The Investigators must decide: (Choose one.)

<bullet> Decide to meet F. at the Cavalier Speakeasy in Arkham.

Proceed to **The Cavalier 1.**

<bullet> Decide to meet GG at the Parker House Hotel in Boston.

Skip to** Parker House 1.**

:::standalone

**The Cavalier 1: ***It takes a bit of time to navigate through the dimly lit alley behind the Saltonstall Street Market before you find the door you need. After a gruff doorman accepts the password from F's message, you are finally welcomed into the Cavalier Speakeasy: a preferred haunt of the O'Bannion gang, tucked neatly away underneath the streets of Southside. There's a small crowd congregating near the bar, swaying to the somber tunes spun by the house jazz band, but the doorman points you to a small booth in the far corner of the room before you can consider joining them.

It takes no time for your contact to sidle up to the booth. The young man slides you a snifter of murky liquor onto the table before settling in across from you, a grim expression of frustration plain on his face. "Hope finding the joint wasn't too much of a hassle," the man rasps, and it's then that you notice the ruddy bandages snaking around his neck. Realization hits you like a truck. Across from you sits the bartender from the Hotel Seasons, the one you last saw bleeding out behind the bar.*

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to **The Cavalier 2.**

:::image-bottom
./images/loic-muzy-couv-berlin.jpg
:::

sections.name: p7
sections.markdown:
:::image-top
./images/karla ortiz.jpg
:::

:::standalone

**The Cavalier 2: ***"Finlay O'Doyle," he croaks, tipping his own glass back. His voice is understandably hoarse. "Thanks for showing up."

Finlay's name sticks out like a sore thumb in the conversation; one shared with Declan O'Doyle, the old man at the center of the Hotel Seasons massacre. "Yeah, yeah. My granddad," he admits with distaste. "I was his watchdog that night, in case things soured. If I'd known the kind of hell he was about to bring down on us with that Mafia cow, I'd have planted him in the ground myself."

"That lowlife broad's the heart of this whole mess." Finlay continues, refilling his now-empty glass from his own flask. "Ana Giuliano. For a while, I thought she was just some wrinkled-up old good-time gal he picked up from Boston. If only I knew what they'd been scheming." Finlay hits the brakes for a moment, letting the weight of his words hang in the air. "She's the reason granddad split from the crew, and the reason everything's gone down the drain ever since. Miss Naomi's had to pull up stakes and go into hiding, and I need your help finding her so we can stand a fighting chance."

You prod Finlay for answers. Why pull you into this mess in the first place? You'd never even met him before the night of the hit. He snorts into his glass. "I wanted you to help me rat out my granddad and Giuliano, of course. In case you weren't aware, you have a rep around this town for fixing hard problems. That's what the dame who answered your phone told me when I gave you that first call---that this was the sort of thing you dealt with all the time."

Your gut twists into a tight knot. If Finlay's story is true, he **had** reached out to you before the Hotel Seasons massacre, but he couldn't be the one who wrote the mysterious invitation you received. Worse still, that means his message was intercepted by someone who had been inside your house. "Now don't look so glum, pal," Finlay says, noticing the expression on your face. "I've got a lead. With your help, we can wrap this up in two shakes. Whenever granddad called Giuliano into town, he'd hole her up in one of our joints. With a bit of luck, we can pick up her scent there. Then, bing, bang, boom: I take Giuliano for a long walk off a short pier, and you get a nice wad of cash. Sound good?" He stretches a hand across the table, the first signs of a grin on his face. Perhaps this meeting didn't answer all of your questions, but maybe Finlay and his info can help you make some sense of all of this.

You take his hand and shake it. *

**Parker House 1:** *The train ride from Arkham is mercifully uneventful. When you step onto the platform at North Station in the heart of Boston's downtown district, it's just a brisk stroll under the glare of neon lights and streetlamps before you arrive at the Parker House Hotel. Inside, the hotel is every bit a work of art as the Seasons, with polished marble floors and sophisticated French décor. You barely have enough time to give your name to the hotelier before you are intercepted by a tall, broad-shouldered man in a black fedora. "Our guest of honor," he grunts. "Come."

The man swiftly leads you to the hotel lounge before taking a post at the doorway, folding his arms menacingly. Inside, a glamorous young woman sits with her back turned to you, idly swirling her champagne in its glass with disaffected elegance as she watches the world outside the window pass by. She cuts a dazzling figure, an effect that is significantly diminished when she takes note of your arrival and opens her mouth to speak. "Thank goodness," she says, with a nasal voice that could crack solid glass. "You made it. Charmed, I'm sure."

You don't have much time for pleasantries, but Giada Giuliano---"Gigi" to her friends---insists on making small talk before she cuts to the chase. You suspect that she's nervous. "We like to solve our problems in-house, capice?" she sighs, sipping her champagne. "We don't usually need to look outside the family if we got an issue, but this time..." Gigi explains that she recently got hitched to her long-term boyfriend, but it's hard not to flinch when you hear her new husband's name. Mobster Jackie Giuliano is one of the most feared men in the Boston underground, and his name carries weight wherever it's printed. The implication hangs in the air, and you ask if she contacted you in hopes of being rescued from her new marriage. "What, save me? From my big galoot? Nah," she laughs. "I need you to save him."*

:::standalone

**Parker House 2: *** As you settle into the plush seat across from Gigi, she pulls out a photograph from her clutch and slides it in front of you. You recognize the stately grand dame in the photo---this was the woman holding court at the head of the O'Bannion party's table at the Hotel Seasons.

The woman in the photograph, explains Gigi, is Ana Giuliano---her new mother-in-law. "Six months ago, she showed up on our doorstep unannounced. Jackie was over the moon to see his good 'ol ma from the old country. Took all of five minutes for her to start acting like she ruled the damn joint, to start filling Jackie's head with ideas. Ideas like staking bigger claims and sending messages with bullets. Taking out the O'Bannions in Arkham would send a message to all our rivals that no one would be able to cross us and live to tell about it." You're forced to concede that wiping out the O'Bannions as a show of force has its own dark logic, though you're surprised that the reasoning behind the attack at the Hotel Seasons is so simple. "Yeah, see, that's the thing," says Gigi, producing a second photograph from her purse. "It sure ain't."

The second photograph in front of you is significantly older and faded, featuring a seaside portrait of a young boy with scabbed knees sitting next to a stern, older woman in a plain dress. "Jackie showed this to me when we first got together, and I never forgot about it," she snarls.

"**That's** Jackie's mother, not whoever this fake is. That's why I need you, understand? Help me figure out how to stop this, how she's got him fooled, before she sends my baby down a one-way street."

Side by side, the two women in the photographs look as different as night and day. If Gigi is telling the truth, there's no way that the women in each photo could be the same person. You lean in to ask how she got wind of you, why she invited you to the Hotel Seasons. "My boys told me you're no greenhorn," she smirks. "Haven't you been solving riddles like this for years? Truth is, I meant to flag you down sooner, but this is the first time I've put out a formal invitation." Gigi pauses to finish off the last of her champagne. "We had to check the papers to see if you even made it through the hotel bloodbath alive. I didn't toss you into that mess, cross my heart." The revelation that Gigi isn't your elusive benefactor is, to say the least, disappointing. She catches the shift in your demeanor and cracks a grin that's equal parts charm and mischief. "Hey, chin up, honey. I'm not about to toss you into another mess unprepared, neither. I know exactly where Ana's holed up, and my boys have paved the way for a smooth operation. Plus, we're talking compensation. Big, fat stacks. You get me?"

Whether or not Gigi is entirely trustworthy remains to be seen---she is, after all, the wife of an underworld kingpin---but the identity of Ana Giuliano may be the key to the mystery you're beginning to unravel. It couldn't hurt to dig a little deeper---especially if the pay is right.*

## Scenario II-A: Behind Closed Doors

**Behind Closed Doors I:** *The Three Conies is a weary-looking tenement building in the underbelly of lower Southside, a part of town kept squarely under the O'Bannions' thumb. Named for the recurring visual motif of tinner's rabbits that appears throughout its architecture, the six-story building still wears its scars from a terrible fire a decade ago. While repairs have been slow, many of its tenants have continued to eke out a comfortable living on its first and second floors for years with the assistance of its devoted landlady, Miss Lila Starett. You aren't surprised to spot the police loitering around the entrance, given the escalated tension between the O'Bannions and their rivals after the Hotel Seasons bloodbath---but after overhearing a pair of officers discussing a series of grisly murders that took place in the building overnight, you quickly realize that their presence is anything but routine.*

**Behind Closed Doors 2:** *Finlay ushers you into the Three Conies through a maintenance entrance in a nearby alleyway, bypassing the police crowding the building's entryway. "Easy does it," he whispers as he holds open the side door for you. "Stick close and keep your head low. If anyone gets nosy, tell them you live here. Act like you own the joint."

As you slink through the dimly lit corridors, the shuffling sound of distant footsteps keeps time with your nerves. It sounds like the building's caretaker is performing her nightly rounds. If you're to find information on Madame Giuliano, you'll need to tread carefully to avoid rousing the tenants' suspicions---and if she turns out to have had anything to do with the murders that took place here, you'll have your work cut out for you.*

**Behind Closed Doors 3:** *You've found yourself jumping at shadows since the moment you stepped off the train at Northside Station. Your journey through Nussbaum Academy left you with an unshakeable feeling of unease---after leaving the bloodbath at the Hotel Seasons behind her, what could Ana Giuliano stand to gain by coming back to Arkham? What could her link to the ramshackle Three Conies apartments possibly be?

The sensation of dread that hits you the second you slip through the building's main entryway nearly sends you reeling. Gigi shoots you a sidelong glance, silently acknowledging the discomfort neither of you can quite put into words. Something is terribly wrong in this place.

"Stop," a nearby voice commands, shocking you back into reality. "I forbid you from entering this building." Miss Lila Starett, the building's caretaker, stands in the center of the foyer before you. You've long understood Miss Lila to be a well-respected and charitable member of Arkham's local community, but the look of sheer hatred on her face stops you in your tracks. "This is not the place for your meddling. You fools think you know everything now, but you have no idea," She hisses, shifting her gaze manically between each of you. Gigi attempts to interject, managing to squeak out an indignant "Listen here, lady-" before she is drowned out by Miss Lila's screaming.

"You see only the shadow of the smoke, not the smoke itself. Not the fire that it comes from, nor what fueled the fire. Let alone who set that fire in the first place." As the building's caretaker continues to rave at you, the sound of gunfire from the floor above you cuts through the night. Lila takes a deep breath and, with all of the strength her tiny frame can muster, lets out one last defiant shriek.

"YOU KNOW NOTHING."

With a speed she shouldn't possibly be capable of, Miss Lila Starett produces a small pistol from her clutch, presses it to her own temple, and pulls the trigger.*

**Resolution 4:** *Finlay sifts through the rubble for what feels like hours, looking for clues that might justify your harrowing visit to the Three Conies. Finally, he calls out to you with an urgent holler. "Take a look at this," Finlay whispers, nodding towards his discovery. Amidst the rubble, a solitary fragment of wall stands upright, adorned with an unblemished painting amidst the decayed wallpaper. The portrait depicts three solemn women seated together, their hands clasped together in a gesture of friendship. A brass plaque at the frame's base identifies them as Lilian Mason, Elizabeth Salmon, and Helena Nussbaum: Proprietresses of the Three Conies Inn. Finlay lets out a weary chuckle. "This is a little too on the nose, if you ask me," he sighs. There's something about the painting's survival amongst the wreckage that's almost comically deliberate.

The following day, Finlay pulls up to your doorstep in his Model T, a mischievous grin on his face. "Hop on in," he says, his eyes sparkling with excitement. "We're going on an adventure." You settle into the back seat as Finlay elaborates. "My boys found nothing on Mason, but Elizabeth Salmon? Turns out she's an old witch that ran an inn the Conies was built on top of. Helena Nussbaum, on the other hand, cleared out of Arkham and opened some kind of ballet school just north of Boston. Miss Naomi always said when it comes to the mumbo jumbo that happens in our town, there's no such thing as coincidences. You up for a dance?" You nod, ready to finally unravel this mystery.

There's a newspaper lying on the seat next to you. It reports on the Hotel Seasons massacre, which the media is now calling the 'Night of Vespers.' You inquire about the name's significance. "Goddamn if I know," Finlay replies, revving the automobile's engine. "It's what Giuliano's people started calling it. Supposed to be some old Italian war or something. Honestly, I never paid much attention in history class."

Finlay flashes his most charming smile at you as the Model T shifts into gear. "Too busy thinking about the future, I guess."*

Whoever orchestrated your involvement in this infernal mystery certainly has a knack for collateral damage. While you're no closer to any answers, perhaps it doesn't really matter anymore. With Madame Giuliano gone, the tensions between the Boston mob and the O'Bannion boys may fizzle out on their own. This terrible resolution to the mystery may be for the best, after all.

But of course, that hope is fleeting. When Gigi returns from the phone booth, her eyes are brimming with tears. "Listen, uh. You've been a big help, and you made good on what I asked you, so, uh... well, I... don't know what to do now," she admits, her voice trembling. "Jackie's missing. Nobody knows where he is, and our boys are going absolutely crackers looking for him. I thought this would be the end of it, but now..." She trails off, burying her face in her hands. ## Scenario II-B: Dancing with Death

**Dancing With Death 1:** *Despite its remote location, the prestigious performing arts school boasts a distinguished reputation in the world of dance and theater. Still, the long drive to Nussbaum Academy is a somber one. Your Model T rumbles along the winding roads, the scenery passing by in a blur of muted autumn colors. There's a sense of tension that hangs in the air as you cross the Ipswich River and into Willowdale Forest, and every tree branch that scratches against your car's windows sets your skin to crawling.*

<bullet><hsp> Check your campaign log.

<bullet><hsp> If *Gigi Giuliano is assisting the investigation*, skip to **Dancing

with Death 2.**

<bullet><hsp> If *Finlay O'Doyle is assisting the investigation*, skip to **Dancing

with Death 3.**

**Dancing with Death 2:** *For her part, Gigi seems largely oblivious to the ominous surroundings, and has spent the past hour meticulously applying makeup in a compact mirror while outlining her plan. The woman claiming to be Ana Giuliano has been using Nussbaum Academy as her base of operations for months, far from the prying eyes of Gigi's trusted associates. While the school would usually be bustling with students at this time of year, she has arranged for a distraction: tickets to the Boston Ballet for the entire faculty, donated in the name of one of Nussbaum Academy's many benefactors. "If everything goes off without a hitch," Gigi explains, puckering her lips as she paints on her lipstick, "we'll waltz in, get some dirt on Mother Darling, and waltz right back out. Easy street. Capisce?"

Under the cover of nightfall, you and Gigi finally arrive at the gates of the cademy. Gigi orders your driver to hide the Model T nearby and wait before joining you at the compound's threshold. With most of the student body away at the theatre at this late hour, you're in a prime position to take advantage of the opportunity to scour the campus for information on Madame Giuliano. *

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to **Setup (v.1).**

**Dancing with Death 3:** *Over the course of the car ride, You and Finlay have crafted a plan for infiltrating the school---in spite of Finlay's initial insistence on approaching with guns blazing. "Yeah, yeah, I know," he says, his knuckles white against the Model T's steering wheel, "You're right. We keep it cool, we have a better shot of pulling this off." Though he has conceded to your better judgment, Finlay's growing anxiety is as palpable a force as the rain on the windshield. It's clear that his mission to find Naomi O'Bannion is the first thing on his mind, and the prospect of failing to do so is beginning to push him towards impulsive action. But as you approach the gates of Nussbaum Academy, it becomes painfully clear that all of your careful strategizing has been for naught. Even from a distance, you can see the plumes of smoke billowing from the scarlet manor's windows, illuminating the building in a fiery blaze. "Ah, goddammit," Finlay curses, his grip tightening on the wheel as he accelerates straight through the school's gates and up the winding driveway. "I really hate this 'no coincidences' shit."

As you slow to a halt, a young woman stumbles from the doorway of the old-world manor in complete hysterics. Her clothes are smudged with ash and dirt, and her disheveled brown hair clings damply to her face. Finlay dashes from the automobile, rushing to catch her as she collapses onto the gravel. "Lady, are you okay!?" He shouts, supporting the girl's weight in his arms. "What the heck is going on here?"

"It's happening again. It's on fire," The girl mumbles, trembling. "It's all going to burn down, just like before." You attempt to reassure her, but her distress only escalates. "Can't you see? Everything around you will become dark, and someone will take your hand. You'll be pleased, not sad -- you'll enjoy moments of incredible brightness." She babbles frantically, and she edges away from you and Finlay, as though fearful of you both. "You see only the shadow of the smoke, not the smoke itself. Not the fire that it comes from, nor what fueled the fire---you don't see death's fingers on your shoulder!!" With a shriek of terror, the girl tears to her feet, and flees abruptly into the woods behind the academy.

You're shaken by the encounter, but Finlay's voice snaps you back to reality. "We can't chase after her," he insists, his tone firm. "If Giuliano's in there, we've got to get her out now, or we'll never be able to put an end to this!" He's right. If Ana Giuliano is the key to quelling the escalating conflict between the mob and the O'Bannion gang, you can't afford to let what she knows go up in smoke.*

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to** Setup (v.2)**

:::resolution

**If no resolution was reached because each investigator was defeated:** *You awaken in a clearing behind the school, to the sensation of rain falling on your cheeks. As you climb to your feet, you can see the charred, skeletal remains of Nussbaum Academy through the trees, the acrid scent of smoke lingering in the air as rain snuffs out the last of the fire. Your bones ache as you climb to your feet, and you prepare to confront the aftermath of your encounter within the school as you slowly begin to make your way back to your automobile.*

<bullet><hsp> Each investigator receives 1 mental trauma.

<bullet><hsp> Check your campaign log.

<bullet> If *Gigi Giuliano is assisting the investigation*, proceed to

**Resolution 3.**

<bullet> If *Finlay O'Doyle is assisting the investigation*, proceed to

**Resolution 4.**

**Resolution 1**: *The cool night air on your face is a relief after your night spent stumbling through the school's labyrinthine corridors. You'd expected your search for Madame Giuliano to unravel the makings of some gangland plot---not the coven of witches you found below the academy. Thankfully, your timely intervention disrupted the occult ritual the coven had been performing; although the academy itself is certainly worse for wear, you've saved the students of Nussbaum Academy from a dreadful fate at the hands of whatever terrible force the witches serve.*

<bullet><hsp> Record in your campaign log that *You stopped the ritual at

Nussbaum Academy*. Add 1 <tablet> to the chaos bag for the remainder

of the campaign.

<bullet><hsp> Any investigator may add the Glass Peacock story asset to their

deck. This asset does not contribute to that investigator's

deck size.

<bullet><hsp> If Olga Safronova, Patricia Simms, and Sarah Pierce are in the

victory display, each investigator gains 1 bonus experience.

<bullet><hsp> If Blanche Pappenheimer is in the victory display, record in your

campaign log that *You deposed the leader of the Nussbaum

Academy Coven.*

<bullet><hsp> Skip to **Resolution 3.**

:::resolution

**Resolution 2: ** *Madame Giuliano's laughter echoes throughout the decadent lair, her hands reaching triumphantly toward the rafters. "Do you think this is over, my children? You have no idea what you're playing at, do you? Not an inkling of what awaits you! You're fumbling, stumbling about in the dark like insects---But at least now, now you see the smoke!"

As if on cue, smoke begins to pour into Madame Giuliano's lair as the fire that has ravaged the academy finally reaches its depths. Ana's hysterical laughter grows louder as bits of the building begin to rain down dangerously around her. Finlay yanks you unceremoniously toward the exit, his grip iron around your wrist. "We've gotta go," he shouts, kicking down the doorway out of Madame Giuliano's room in one swift motion. "I'm not letting us die in here!"

When you make your way out of the dark boudoir, the last you see of Madame Giuliano is her face twisted in manic delight, just before she is overtaken by the falling debris.*

<bullet><hsp> Record in your campaign log that *You dealt with Madame

Giuliano.*  Add 1 <elder_thing> to the chaos bag for the remainder of

the campaign.

<bullet><hsp> If all three Binding Charms are in the victory display, each

investigator earns 2 bonus experience.

<bullet><hsp> Skip to **Resolution 4.**

**Resolution 3**: *Given that your search turned up no sign of Madame Giuliano, you'd expected Gigi to show some disappointment. Instead, she's pleased as punch, wearing a self-satisfied grin on her face as she fishes a cigarette from her purse. "Did you want a smoke too?" She says, once she notices you looking her way. "Sorry, doll. It's the last one I got." You have half a mind to ask Gigi what she could possibly be in such a good mood about when she produces a folded sheet of paper from her handbag and nonchalantly presses it into your palm. "I found this inside. Anything strike ya as familiar?"

Your eyes widen when you realize what you're holding---it's a handwritten invitation, penned by Declan O'Doyle, addressed to Madame Giuliano herself. "Lay low, my love, and wait for me at our special place," it reads, accompanied by a peculiar illustration of three hares arranged in a wheel. It's a strange symbol, but one you recognize---you know that this circular motif is called the Tinner's Rabbits. You know this because it's displayed prominently across the architecture of the Three Conies, a long-standing tenement building in Arkham's Southside. Everyone in Arkham knows about the Three Conies. Gigi smirks when you explain this to her and puffs a cloud of smoke into the night air. "Guess I'm heading on over to your neck of the woods. Think I can count on you to show me around?"

:::resolution

The following day, as you and Gigi prepare to depart on the train to Arkham from Boston's North Station, you find your attention drawn by a radio broadcast playing in the station cafe. The announcer's voice crackles as he recounts the grisly events of the massacre at the Hotel Seasons in Arkham, dubbing it the "Night of Vespers." You look over your shoulder at Gigi, hoping she'll be able to shed some light on the unusual name. "It's an old rebellion where they ran the French out of Sicily," she explains, her tone tinged with exasperation as she steps aboard the train. "The name is Mother Darling's work, no doubt. It's got her brand of old-world charm written all over it." Gigi settles into her seat opposite you, gazing out the window to the platform in quiet contemplation. Eventually, she can't help but voice her thoughts aloud.

"Honestly, who in their right mind would pick Sicily over Paris?"*

of each card in the victory display.

Doors.** (p. 8)

**Resolution 4:** *There's a dark cloud hanging over Finlay by the time you both reach his automobile. While attempting to deal with Madame Giuliano may have spared Finlay the guilt of leaving his grandfather's mess unattended, you learned nothing of use from her. Naomi is still missing. What's more, Nussbaum Academy's destruction is likely to only exacerbate the war Madame Giuliano started. In a moment of frustration, Finlay slams his fist against the dashboard, the sound reverberating through the car. He lets out a loud curse and shakes the sting from his knuckles with immediate regret. "Sorry," he mumbles sadly, though you think the apology might be intended for his car.

Finlay starts the automobile. "Let's go home. We'll... we'll plan our next step on the way," he says, feebly attempting to mask the growing feeling of defeat that hangs in the air between you. "We'll think of something. We gotta."

Weary and exhausted, you and Finlay embark on the long drive back to Arkham. A night of rest will do you both some good.*

## Interlude II: The Rose of Tuscany

**Interlude 1: ***You're bone-tired by the time you finally get home. The events of the past few days have drained you to the core. Your mind is cluttered with thoughts of Nussbaum Academy and the Three Conies, but you're too fatigued to make much sense of them. By the time you're inside your own room, the relief of returning home is such a comfort that you almost miss the dim glow of the lit cigar in the shadows.

You aren't alone. Your hand moves instinctively to your coat pocket, but a smoky laugh cuts through the silence. "You stop that. It's bad manners," says a woman's voice. "And I've been waiting for you all night. Turn your lights on. I'm tired of sitting in the dark."

When the lights turn on, a stern-looking woman in a shabby coat sits across the room from you, seated in your chair. Dark circles mark her heavy-lidded eyes, and tangled strands of wet hair cascade around her shoulders like a lion's mane. She extinguishes her cigar on your windowsill, ignoring your protestations. "You and I have quite a bit to discuss," she says, speaking in an accent you can't quite place. "Sit, now. Time is not a luxury we are afforded."

Although there is something about this woman's pompous way of speaking that almost compels you to follow her instructions, you're not about to let an intruder dictate terms to you in your own home. You demand to know her identity, what she wants, and how she managed to get inside. "You are inane. How does anyone get anywhere?" she answers blithely, rolling her eyes at you. "How did any of us arrive at this moment? Fate, perhaps? You opened the door and walked inside. It will make you feel better to think that I did, too." She allows the silence to linger for a long, frustrating moment before she inhales sharply through her nose in exasperation.

"I am Maddalena Talenti," she declares, in a tone usually reserved for royalty. "You received an invitation to dine at the Hotel Seasons some days ago. I sent this invitation to you. I wished for you to bear witness to the events that are now unfolding."*

<bullet><hsp> If an investigator in the campaign is playing Agatha Crane, Dexter

Drake, Edith Foster, Gloria Goldberg, Kohaku Narukami, Mandy

Thompson, Daisy Walker, or Harvey Walters, choose one of them to

read **The Name of the Rose** below. Otherwise, skip to **Interlude 2.**

:::standalone

**The Name of the Rose:** *You've heard that name before. The late American folklorist Charles Godfrey Leland claimed to have learned much of his comprehensive knowledge on witchcraft from an elderly peasant woman in Tuscany named Maddalena Talenti. However, Leland passed over twenty years ago, and the Maddalena he knew would be positively ancient by now. This pompous young woman before you simply does not match up with the woman Leland described.*

<bullet><hsp> Record in your campaign log that your investigator "*knows the Name of the Rose.*" You (and only you) gain 2 bonus experience.

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to **Interlude 2.**

:::

**Interlude 2:*** Suddenly, there is scratching at your window. Behind Maddalena, you glimpse the dark, ominous outlines of birds---ravens, perhaps--- beating their wings against the glass in a frenzy. Maddalena's stern demeanor falters, giving way to a look of genuine fear. "We have been found," she gasps. "We must go now. We are in grave danger."

You begin to demand answers to your growing barrage of questions: Who has tracked you down? What is going on, and where is the explanation you are due?

But Maddalena simply presses her thumb against your forehead, and with a single, decisive push, you're sent reeling---and suddenly you are no longer in your room, but somewhere altogether different. A desolate place, draped in darkness, beneath an infinite, starless sky.*

<bullet><hsp> Proceed to **Scenario 3: The Teachings of Aradia.**

## Scenario 3: The Teachings of Aradia

**Intro 1:** *The bleak, alien expanse that stretches out before you is something out of a nightmare. Icy winds lash against your face as you struggle to orient yourself in this barren, rain-slick wasteland. Your ability to see through the darkness comes in flashes, illuminated only by the distant flicker of lightning from the empty sky above. Maddalena, who stood beside you only moments ago in the comfort of your room, is nowhere to be found.*

<bullet><hsp> If an investigator in the campaign has the <t>Dreamer</t>, <t>Sorcerer</t>, or <t>Witch</t> trait, choose one of them to read **Deja Vu** below. Otherwise, skip to **Intro 2.**

:::standalone

**Deja Vu:*** There’s something about this strange place that strikes you as oddly familiar. You’re no stranger to the otherworldly, and there's a strange quality in the tension of the air that reminds you of the lands just beyond the veil of sleep---similar, somehow, but distinct enough to make you deeply uncomfortable. You’re experienced enough in the occult arts to know when you’ve crossed that particular threshold, and you’re quite sure that you're awake.

But if you aren't in the Dreamlands, then where?*

<bullet><hsp> Search your deck for an asset that takes up at least 1 arcane slot.

<hsp>You may put that asset into play, at no cost. Proceed to **Intro 2.**

:::

**Intro 2:*** Another flash of lightning illuminates the sky, and you see it---the unmistakable silhouette of a white owl, perched atop an outcropping of jagged stone nearby. As you strain to get a better look at it, the first sign of life in this desolate place, Maddalena's voice rings out in your mind as clearly as a bell.

"Ah, good. I've found you," she says. "Follow the owl."*

### <color #000000>Veiled</color>

Many of the locations in both The Teachings of Aradia and subsequent scenarios in the campaign will have the veiled keyword. Instead of an unrevealed side, these locations have story cards on their reverse sides.

Whenever a location with the veiled keyword enters play (including

during setup), place clues on that location equal to its clue value, as

normal. This keyword represents that a location contains unknown lore or assistance that must be sought out by the investigators before it can be of use to them.

As a <free> ability, an investigator at a veiled location with no clues

on it may flip that location over, resolving the text on its other side.

**Once a veiled location has been flipped over and its story text has been read, it cannot be flipped over again for the remainder of the

game unless otherwise noted.**

:::standalone

:::

**If no resolution was reached because each investigator was defeated, and it was Act 1 when the scenario ended:** Skip to **Resolution 2.**

:::resolution

**If no resolution was reached because each investigator was defeated, and it was Act 2 when the scenario ended:** Skip to **Resolution 3.**

**Resolution 1:*** Through sheer grit and determination, you have managed to fend off the relentless assault of the Three Mothers' thralls. You find Maddalena slumped against a wall, and though her face is pale and drawn from exhaustion, she wears a smug grin. "I knew I was right to bet on you," she says pridefully, as if she had not just spent the bulk of her strength to maintain the barrier around her sanctuary.

"There is no turning back now," she says, pulling herself to her feet. "The Three Mothers know you. They will come for you, and they will stop at nothing until they claim you, or your life... both, perhaps, should they feel particularly offended. They do so like to take offense, you know." Maddalena produces a piece of chalk from her pocket and begins to sketch a complex pattern upon the wall. "We return to my original plan, then," She says, continuing her work. "We eliminate the Three Mothers once and for all, before they can claim their vengeance upon you."

It's hard not to feel overwhelmed by doubt when you ask Maddalena how she expects you to contend against the Three Mothers---entities that she herself claims are immortal and endless. With a wave of her hand, Maddalena's owl companion swoops down to perch on your shoulder. "Stolas is a capricious little thing, but he will aid you as long as I wish him to," she explains. "Through his eyes, I will protect you from harm and guide your hand." With a flourish, Maddalena completes her drawing and a shimmering portal appears in its place. The familiar image of your room is visible just beyond the threshold.

"Time presses on. Return home and make your preparations, as I shall do here. Learn as much as you can about the Three Mothers. You will find that they are not without their weaknesses."

You feel a sudden pang of regret---regret for ever breaking the seal on that letter. It's a feeling you've become all too familiar with since that innocuous invitation arrived. You'd been promised a simple evening out on the town, and now the peril you find yourself in is beyond anything you could have imagined. Three immortal, powerful witches are lurking out there in the darkness, and thanks to Maddalena's scheming, you've become a pawn in her deadly game against them---a game you cannot help but play, and one you have little chance of winning. You step through the portal home, and Maddalena calls out as it closes behind you. "Trust in me," she says, and the steady confidence in her voice is almost enough to soothe your fears. "I will see you through this storm."*

<bullet><hsp> Record in your campaign log that "*The Long Quiet Stands*."

<bullet><hsp> One investigator must add the Great Prince Stolas: 36th Spirit of

**Resolution 2: *** You wake to the sound of rain pounding against the earth. Your surroundings slowly come into focus: you are propped up against an unmarked headstone in the desolate potter's field just north of West Derby Street. You try to piece together the events that led you here. The last thing you remember was chasing after Maddalena's owl, through that terrible, cold expanse. Had that been a dream?

A flash of lightning cracks the sky, and déjà vu strikes like a slap across your face. There is Maddalena's owl, perched on a broken stone cross not twenty yards away. It swoops down, landing in front of you on the rain-soaked dirt. Not a dream, then.

The owl stares up at you with its beady eyes, and Maddalena's voice rings out once more in your mind. "Time is running short," she says, her voice tinged with urgency. "I have misplayed my hand, and now we are all in great danger. I... am sorry."

"I will do my best to guide you. If you wish to survive, you must know your enemy. Learn as much as you can about the Three Mothers---they are your pursuers, and they will not stop until you are dead. Take my Familiar, Stolas; I---" Maddalena's voice falters, distracted. "I must go."

The rain pelts down relentlessly from the sky above, soaking you to the bone. What in the world has this woman dragged you into? You pull yourself to your feet, and Maddalena's owl---Stolas, apparently---flutters up to perch upon your shoulder. As bewildered as you are, Maddalena's warning was clear: whoever or whatever the Three Mothers are, they mean you harm, and you must learn as much as you can about the Three Mothers before they catch you unprepared.*

<bullet><hsp> Record in your campaign log that "*The Long Quiet Fell*."

Randomly add 1 <cultist>, 1 <tablet>, or 1 <elder_thing> to the chaos bag for the

remainder of the campaign.

Victory Display.

<bullet><hsp> The mystery continues in **Interlude III: The Three Mothers.**

:::resolution

**Resolution 3:** *With a resounding groan, the barrier protecting the Long Quiet gives way. It collapses with a crash, and torrential rain and biting wind are unleashed upon the sanctuary's halls. With the wards broken, the phantasmal spectres drawn from the abyss begin to drift toward the interior of the sanctum. The Long Quiet has been lost.

"No," Maddalena gasps, her breath ragged with exhaustion. Despite her weariness, she bursts into feverish, mysterious chanting as she hastily etches a complex pattern onto the stone wall beside you with a piece of chalk. "The Three Mothers know you now," she says, her voice tense with urgency. "They will find you and kill you one thousand times over, unless you do exactly as I say. Take my familiar, Stolas; return to your world and arm yourself with knowledge. If you wish to survive, you must know them, in turn." Maddalena completes her drawing with a final flourish, and a shimmering portal appears in its place. Beyond lies the familiar sight of your own room. "Move quickly. I'll assist as best I can, but you cannot stay here. They'll be upon us before long---but I must remain here. The Long Quiet cannot be allowed to fall."

With Maddalena's owl perched on your shoulder, she gives you a solemn push through the portal before it seals shut behind you. Her parting words echo in your mind as you cross the threshold: "I'm sorry. I did not want this."*

## Interlude III: The Three Mothers

**Interlude 1: *** The task before you is daunting. To survive their wrath, you must learn all you can about the Three Mothers---the three immortal witches that lie at the root of this mystery. Maddalena's cryptic explanations of their true nature while you journeyed through The Long Quiet did much to underscore the terrifying scope of their power and sinister goals, but any actual knowledge you have of who they are and what they want from you is frustratingly slim.

Though Maddalena had promised to stay in contact through her familiar, Stolas, you haven't heard a single word from her. The owl itself has been little more than a nuisance, leaving a trail of feathers and filth around your home, but you're not about to let Maddalena's silence or her pet's poor behavior deter you. With a weary determination, you begin to explore your options. *

<bullet><hsp> Each player must choose a passage to read that applies to their

investigator to begin uncovering the mystery of the Three Mothers.

Once each investigator has read a passage, skip to** Interlude 2.**

:::standalone

If your investigator has the <t>Detective, Police, or Warden</t> trait: *With the O'Bannion Gang and the Boston Mob butting heads, your contacts at the Arkham Police Department are stretched thin trying to keep peace on the streets. One alarming report stands out amongst the others as you search through the precinct's records; a mirror image of the murders that followed in the wake of the Hotel Seasons' fire are playing out in real-time on the streets of San Francisco, clear across the country. The victims, all mowed down in classic gangland style, all have one thing in common: a membership to the Tenebrarum Lodge, a local gentleman's club. You swallow the lump in your throat. Tenebrarum. That can't be a coincidence. With a quick glance over your shoulder, you stash the report away in your coat pocket.*

Tenebrarum Murders.*

If your investigator has the <t>Assistant, Miskatonic, Scholar, or Wayfarer</t> trait:*  When you decide to seek out the wisdom of your dear friend Dr. Henry Armitage, the head of Miskatonic University's Orne Library, he is delighted to oblige. He arrives at your doorstep carrying a stack of heavy books, which he deposits in your arms with a grunt. "Thomas de Quincy's Suspiria de Profundis should be a fair jumping off point," Armitage wheezes, wiping his brow with a handkerchief. "But after that, you'll want to delve into Our Ladies of Sorrow by Brother Ross."

You find that Suspiria de Profundis is mostly poetic drivel, waxing lyrical about the Three Mothers in vague, flowery prose. It paints them as metaphors for human suffering, rather than actual entities, and provides little in the way of concrete information. Brother Ross's book is an entirely different beast. A sixteenth-century account by a Welsh monk scrawled on delicate, yellowed pages, Our Ladies of Sorrow is a detailed collection of historical events that Ross claims are the devilish work of the Three Mothers.

"The Sorrows, or Our Ladies of Sorrow, are dreadful spirits from the dawn of man, ageless and endless. They may be daughters of Lilith, although they sometimes exhibit a compassion for mankind that the Queen of Night lacks. Or they may be kin to grim Hecate, though they do not shun the daylight as she does. They may be three, or they may merely be one. There are hundreds of legends about them, in their multitude of forms. Which of these stories are closest to the truth is anyone's guess." *

The only other thing that you've managed to retain from your dreamlike haze is the memory of sitting beneath a majestic chestnut tree on top of a hill, staring out across a moonlit bay.

It's not until later the next day, when you stumble upon a photograph in one of your books, that it suddenly all clicks. The hill with the tree, overlooking the ocean---your dreams had taken you to the faraway Gulf of Naples in Italy. You don't know why, but somehow, you're absolutely certain that you'll find a key to unlocking this mystery in that very bay.*

You've been nursing a glass of whiskey at the bar for half an hour when the conversation you've been eavesdropping on takes an intriguing turn. "Can you believe it?" one of the two women says, leaning in conspiratorially to her friend. "After all these years, Madame Nussbaum is going back to Germany. Who will run the school, I wonder?" You feign disinterest, but your mind is racing---Helena Nussbaum, the elusive and mysterious headmistress of Nussbaum Academy, should have known about the coven of witches you found deep in the bowels of her school... it stands to reason that she would be a link back to the Three Mothers as well.

The other woman, clearly drunk, chides her friend. "Don't be stupid, Suzy. Madame Nussbaum never leaves Freiburg. Madame Pappenheimer runs the school in her place. Everyone knows that." You lean back, letting their words sink in. This is more than idle chatter---this is a lead.

You polish off the last of your drink. Perhaps it's time for you to pay Helena herself a visit.*

If your investigator has the <t>Agency, Medic, Reporter, or Veteran</t> trait: *A nagging suspicion has been gnawing at the back of your mind ever since you lost contact with Maddalena. You can't shake the feeling that you've heard of something like this before. You're reminded of an account you heard of long ago, during your training: something about a veteran, returned from the war, but what was it? Driven by instinct, you arrange to visit the department of records at Arkham Sanitarium. It's only a few hours into your search before you find the dusty records on Patient #84762: Sergeant Frank Mandel.

You thumb through the pages, and pieces of the puzzle begin to fall into place. Sgt. Mandel had been a decorated soldier, but he had returned from his post near Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany, as a man shattered. His file is a catalogue of horrors, filled with sketches of spectral figures and twisted corpses rendered in a trembling hand. Your heart quickens as you turn to the final entry in Mandel's diary. It's all here---the same dread, the same sense of impending doom that hangs heavy above your own head.

"Ever since we met in the Black Forest, I see her all the time. I hear her terrible whispers. My own secrets revealed to me, and hers as well. **Mother**. All she wants, she says, is to be embraced, loved. Known.

But to know her is to give up my soul. God, forgive me.

She claims to grieve, but her sorrow is a knife.

She claims to love, but her love is the abyss.

**s u s p i r i o r u m**”*
